research.summary:
Since January 2026 the AI-story manifestation niche has filled up quickly. Stella (4.72 stars, 5,346 ratings, released 2026-01-28, #100 in Health & Fitness) has prompted near-copies within months: Aya (4.80, 3,217 ratings, April 2026), Future You, Daya, Magnetic, Calyn, Already Done, Demi and Plasti. Almost all of them make you answer a long, personal questionnaire and then put the app behind a weekly paywall ($4.99–$9.99 a week), and several also sell credits or individual audios. In the most recent US reviews (pulled through Apple's review feed), 35% of Stella's reviews are 1–2 stars (156 of 441). By rough keyword count, 132 of those mention paying or price and 60 mention the invasive questions. Aya's rate is 46%. Vela's best defence is therefore what it already has: generous free use, everything kept on the phone, no account and no weekly plan. But the current screenshots and screens don't show any of this, and the app looks text-only and thin next to competitors.

What reviewers love is emotional realism built from personal details ("the first story made me cry"), stories that work as background listening (driving, gym, sleep), soft narration with music, home/lock-screen widgets, streaks, and recording affirmations in your own voice. What they keep asking for is loop/replay/playlist, longer stories, background playback, stories they can edit, correct pronunciation of names, and more inclusive imagery. Stella reviewers complain the images are "all rich white girls", and Moonly is losing ratings over "AI slop" (77 of 317 recent low-star reviews mention AI). Visually the category splits in two: pastel pink/lilac with stock photos of women in headphones (Stella, Aya, Future You, Daya, Calyn), and dark cosmic indigo or black-and-gold (Soul, Vix, Magnetic, Innertune). Vela's indigo and gold already sits in the second group, so it has to stand out through what it does, not its colours.

Most competitors now have a "proof wall" or "manifestation board", but these are passive logs of signs and outcomes. None of them links one daily action to proof that changes the next story. That gap is real and is exactly Vela's Future Memory loop, so new features should deepen it. Vela should not add anything from the crowded zones: "meet/hear your future self" with photo swipes, winning back a specific person or ex, subliminals and frequencies, tarot/moon/astrology (Apple's guideline 4.3(b) names fortune telling as saturated), AI coach chat, voice cloning, or "#1 app" laurels and testimonial screenshots. Shine is no longer a competitor: it was pulled from both stores by April 2023 after Headspace bought it.

findings.title: The AI-story category punishes 'long questionnaire, then paywall'. Vela's free, on-device model is its strongest edge, but nothing shows it
findings.detail: Every AI-story competitor asks a long, personal questionnaire and then locks the app: Stella ($6.99/week, plans from $6.99 to $79.99), Aya ($9.99/week, $29.95/month, $149.99/year, plus $1.99 per audio, $4.99 per playlist and 3 or 15 'instant episode' credit packs), Future You (subscription required, plus '5 Refine Stars $9.99' and '40 Stars $49.99'), Daya ('3-day free trial, then $7.99/week'), Already Done ($4.99/week, $99.99/year), Magnetic (Premium+ $132.99/year, plus à-la-carte 'songs'). In the most recent US App Store reviews, 156 of Stella's 441 are 1–2 stars (35%); by rough keyword count, 132 of those mention paying or price and 60 mention the questions or personal data. Aya: 21 of 46 recent reviews are 1–2 stars, many saying the paywall cut in mid-audio. Typical quotes: 'interrogated me for 20 minutes and then asked for money' (Stella); '$336 a year for an app that isn't a guarantee'; 'Why does a manifestation app need to know if I have children, where I live'; 'Made me fill out 39 questions then asked for money' (Daya); 'if I am already paying $29.99 why do I need to pay an additional fee' (Aya); 'stories I had access to yesterday are already disappearing… limited to two story edits before being charged' (Future You). Calyn (released 2026-08-27, $5.99/month, $39.99/year) already copies the 'your answers stay on your device' privacy pitch, so privacy alone is not unique. It has to be paired with the loop.
findings.evidence: Stella listing https://apps.apple.com/us/app/-/id6757347283 (4.7, 5.3K ratings, #100 H&F, IAP list); Aya, Future You, Daya, Magnetic, Calyn and Already Done IAP sections on apps.apple.com/us/app/id6760195623, id6762685636, id6802366942, id6758529128, id6803900385, id6760242662; iTunes Search API counts (Stella 5,346; Aya 3,217; Future You 262; Daya 69); review RSS feeds https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/page=N/id=<id>/sortby=mostrecent/json, combined in C:\Users\GAINJO~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Gain-John-Downloads-solve-problem\f6853cbe-5ed2-4f58-8cba-218452638bb6\scratchpad\reviews_all.json; Daya description ('$7.99/week'); Calyn description ('Your answers stay on your device').
findings.implication_for_vela: Put the promise at the front. One screenshot and the onboarding should say plainly: 'Your story is free. Unlimited listens. No account, no servers, no weekly plan, no credits.' Keep onboarding at 6 steps or fewer and keep showing the first chapter before any paywall. Promise that anything a user made stays readable if Plus lapses (Aya and Future You get punished for this). Never move a free feature behind the paywall later: Manifest (Transcend) did and got 'used to be way better… everything is behind a paywall'.

findings.title: Reviewers praise emotional realism and background listening, and keep asking for a better player
findings.detail: The most common Stella praise: 'The first story immediately made me cry'; 'It makes the best mind movies!'; 'I play these stories while I clean'; 'Fall asleep to them every night'; 'listening while I'm driving, at the gym'; 'You can even use your own voice and I love that'; 'background music while you listen'. Stella's site sells personal details ('your name, people you love') and ambient soundscapes (rain, café, ocean). Requests from 3–4 star reviews: loop and replay ('I wish it had a loop button'; 'continuously loop the tracks'), queue or playlist ('a special playlist so a person can listen to them as a series whether they're sleeping'), longer stories ('Currently ~3 mins. 6–10 mins would be perfect'), no auto-advance, playback that continues with the screen off, editable story lines and titles, editable profile, correct name pronunciation ('it can't pronounce my name right'), wrong-gender details breaking immersion ('constantly refers to one of my sons as a daughter… kills the vibe'), regenerating sooner than every 24 hours, and dark/light mode. A keyword scan found 16 loop/playlist/longer requests among Stella's 3–5 star reviews and 32 for Innertune. Innertune's positive reviews centre on 'listen every night on repeat'. Vix shipped a loop and sleep timer after reviewers complained. Innertune is criticised for 'robotic' or 'phony AI' voices, which matters because Vela uses device TTS through expo-speech (the repo has no audio library, no recording and no sleep timer).
findings.evidence: Stella reviews in the RSS feed (2026-05 to 2026-10); downloadstella.com feature list; Innertune listing https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6443625379 ('19 voices… 100+ beats', 4.85/11,976) and its reviews; Vix version notes 1.11 and 1.22 (loop, sleep timer, lock-screen controls) at https://apps.apple.com/app/id6747910148; Vela package.json (expo-speech only; no expo-audio or widget target).
findings.implication_for_vela: Make the chapter a real listening experience: background playback with lock-screen controls, sleep timer, loop chapter, 'play my arc' (all chapters of a dream in a row), a Short (about 3 minutes) or Deep (6–8 minutes) length choice, original ambient sound beds (bundled, self-made or CC0), a voice picker that prefers enhanced/premium system voices, a 'how to say my name' field, an optional 'people in my story' list with pronouns, and tap-to-edit any line, with edits remembered by the engine. Every one of these runs on the device at no cost.

findings.title: Photos of people and AI-generated imagery now hurt ratings. Original generative art would set Vela apart and avoids both problems
findings.detail: Stella's visuals are AI-style lifestyle photos, and they draw recurring complaints: 'out of all the hundreds of pictures it's all rich white girls'; 'mostly slim blonde white women so it's hard to pretend it's me'; 'I can't relate to a rich white girl or a rich white couple'; 'Would love less ai generated pictures and more customization in terms of the aesthetic'; queer users say the images are 'of straight couples'. Moonly (4.64 stars, 31,403 ratings) is losing reviews over generative AI: 317 of its 500 most recent US reviews are 1–2 stars, and 77 of those mention AI, generation, 'slop' or robots ('Now it's cluttered with so much AI slop'; a 5-star review in Russian says it 'was cool when illustrations weren't AI-generated'). The AI-story apps' screenshots almost all use stock photos of young women in headphones (Aya, Future You, Daya, Plasti 'Picture the life you want').
findings.evidence: Stella reviews 2026-07-31, 2026-09-03, 2026-09-06, 2026-09-17, 2026-10-07 (RSS feed); Moonly listing https://apps.apple.com/US/app/id1489889871 and its review feed; App Store screenshot galleries for Aya (id6760195623), Future You (id6762685636), Daya (id6802366942) and Plasti (id6745577856), viewed in the browser.
findings.implication_for_vela: Don't add stock or AI photos of people. Build an on-device generative art system with react-native-svg or Skia, seeded by each dream's ID: a night sky or 'chapter plate' per dream whose stars are your actual proofs, with the dream's area changing the palette or atmosphere. It is inclusive by design, costs nothing, can't be mistaken for the pastel-photo look, and gives the screenshots the visual richness they currently lack.

findings.title: Every competitor's 'proof wall' is a passive log. None links one daily action to proof that rewrites the next story
findings.detail: The niche has adopted proof boards: Stella's 'Wall of Manifestations', Magnetic's 'MANIFESTATION PROOF BOARD — Track every sign, every synchronicity', Future You's 'manifestation wall', Aya's manifestations log ('keeps the receipts for goals you've listed'), and Vix's 'sign tracking'. All of them record what came true or what 'signs' appeared after the fact, and none feeds back into the content. In vision-board apps, users explicitly ask for the missing link: 'Disappointing: No link between Vision Board and goal… I paid $19.99… I used the app to link the goals to th…' (Vision Board & Goal Tracker, 4.73 stars, 3,758 ratings, 28 of 66 recent reviews 1-star). Unlimits ('one personalized daily action instead of long plans') is a 4-rating AI coach. Plasti's 'Practice first. Then your phone' locks apps; it is not an action-proof loop. Look-back value is real too: a Gratitude review says 'It lifts me up when I review my entries'.
findings.evidence: downloadstella.com ('Wall of Manifestations'); Magnetic description (iTunes lookup id6758529128); Future You description (id6762685636); Aya Google Play promo ('keeps the receipts'); Vix version notes ('sign tracking'); Vision Board & Goal Tracker review 2026-03-16 (RSS id1668760976); Unlimits listing https://apps.apple.com/us/app/unlimits/id6739521906; Gratitude reviews (id1372575227).
findings.implication_for_vela: This is Vela's unserved, defensible space, and the loop that passed 4.3 review. Invest in: (1) a per-dream star map where each logged proof becomes a named star; tap it to see the sentence and the chapter line it changed; (2) a visible 'what changed because of you' highlight inside the next chapter; (3) a monthly 'Evidence reel' or 'Chapter replay' assembled on the device; (4) 'On this day' resurfacing; (5) linking board photos to chapters (pinned images become scene anchors and can be attached as proof photos). Avoid the words 'proof board/wall', 'signs' and 'synchronicities', which already belong to Magnetic and Stella.

findings.title: Table stakes Vela is missing: widgets, a forgiving streak, own-voice recording, ambient sound, image sharing
findings.detail: WIDGETS: the two category giants grew on widgets. I am – Daily Affirmations (4.83 stars, 735,315 ratings; screenshots say 'Customizable widgets', 'Daily reminders', '1000+ themes', '75+ categories', 'Keep a daily practice streak'; also on Apple Watch) and Motivation (4.82 stars, 1,075,042 ratings, #27 H&F, subtitle 'Inspirational positive widgets'). Soul ('YOUR widget, YOUR reality'), Demi ('VISION WIDGET'), Plasti, Vix, Myla and Moonly all have them; Moonly users write 'PLEASE ADD MORE WIDGETS'; Vision Board ++ users complain the widget shows only one tile. STREAKS keep people coming back, and losing one triggers anger: I am reviewers cite 400–510-day streaks; 'Had over a year long streak… The only thing that kept me coming back was the streak' (1 star); Gratitude: 'This app shames you for missing one day! I had 107 days…' (1 star). OWN VOICE: ThinkUp (4.75 stars, 7,515 ratings: 'Record in the voice your brain truly trusts'), Innertune, Aya ('read-aloud affirmations that listen back'), Repetition, Plasti and Already Done. AMBIENT/MUSIC: Stella, Innertune ('100+ beats'), Myla (frequencies), and Vision Board: Dream & Manifest, which added presentation-mode music. SHARING: I am and Manifest (ZipoApps) share designed images in portrait or square. Vela has a streak chip, reminders, plain-text sharing (Share.share) and Listen through expo-speech; it has no widgets, no recording, no ambient sound and no image sharing.
findings.evidence: apps.apple.com/us/app/874656917 (listing and screenshots); apps.apple.com/app/876080126; Soul and Demi descriptions (iTunes lookup 6463946050, 6763245058); I am reviews 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-09 (RSS); Gratitude review 2026-06-01; ThinkUp lookup 906660772; Vision Board: Dream & Manifest notes https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6757963805; Vela source (grep: no widget, audio recording or ambient code; Share.share text only in app/affirmations.tsx).
findings.implication_for_vela: Add an iOS widget set that serves the loop: a 'Today's bridge' widget (the action, tapping opens the proof check-in), a 'Constellation' widget (your star map), and a lock-screen 'carry a line' widget. No competitor has an action-and-proof widget. Make the streak forgiving: count 'nights in your arc' with grace days and never show a shaming reset to zero. Add on-device own-voice recording of your bridge sentence or favourite chapter line (expo-audio). Don't use Apple's Personal Voice API: Apple says it is meant primarily for assistive-communication apps. Add designed share images of a chapter line or your constellation, not just text.

Aya (lilac): 'Manifest Your Dream Self', 'Custom audio visualizations from your future self', 'Tailor-made Subliminals', 'Custom-Made Playlists', 'Create Your Manifestation Board'. Daya (pink): 'Call Someone Into Your Life', 'Subliminals Shift Your Subconscious'. Calyn (pink): sticker collage, 'Written for you', Library. findings.title: Things Vela must NOT copy (guideline 4.3 similarity zones)
findings.detail: Apple's current guideline 4.3(b) rejects apps 'indistinguishable from what's already widely available' and names fortune telling as a saturated type. Vela's own resubmission (store/REVIEW_RESPONSE_4_3.md) won approval by arguing that the action, proof and adaptive-narrative loop is the product and the rituals are only supporting. Features that are now generic across many apps: (1) 'future self' voice or photo framing (Stella 'Meet your future self', Aya 'from your future self', Future You 'Hear your future self', Already Done 'Hear your future self in your own voice', Daya 'Step into your future self'); (2) winning back a specific person or ex (Vix 'Get Your Person back… Make Him Obsessed… Watch Him Come Back', Magnetic 'Your SP' and an IAP called 'Become His Only Option', Daya 'Call Someone Into Your Life'); (3) subliminals, binaural beats, Solfeggio frequencies (Aya, Vix, Magnetic, Daya, Myla, Innertune, VibeSesh, SelfMade); (4) tarot, moon rituals, astrology, lucky numbers (Moonly, Vix daily tarot and moon home screen, Demi 'lucky number', 'Manifest: 369 Moon Ritual'), which falls into the fortune-telling category Apple names; (5) AI chat coach or teacher (Manifest by Transcend, Unlimits, Endly 'Chat with Teacher'); (6) a swipe affirmation deck or 369 as the headline feature (Myla, Vix '369 and 5x55', Magnetic '10 cards a day', Demi); (7) AI voice cloning (Plasti, Already Done, Self Empower Daily), which also conflicts with Vela's no-server rule; (8) proof walls of 'signs and synchronicities' (Magnetic, Vix). Calyn's copy ('not a vision board maker and not a journal… it writes and it narrates') shows how quickly identical positioning appears.
findings.evidence: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (section 4.3); Vix screenshots and version notes https://apps.apple.com/app/id6747910148; Magnetic IAP list ('Become His Only Option $5.99') and description; Daya screenshots; Demi description (iTunes lookup 6763245058); Apple's Personal Voice guidance (https://wwdcnotes.com/notes/wwdc23/10033, https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/736335); C:\Users\Gain John\Downloads\solve_problem\vela\store\REVIEW_RESPONSE_4_3.md.
findings.implication_for_vela: Treat every feature as either deepening the loop (imagine, act, prove, adapt) or as a supporting ritual that feeds it. Rule of thumb: if the feature works without the user doing something in the real world, it probably drifts toward the generic category. Keep affirmations, 369 and gratitude in a secondary tab. Steer away from specific-person romance goals. Don't add moon or tarot content. In store copy, describe the product by its loop, not as 'manifestation stories'.

findings.title: Delight mechanics behind high ratings: small ceremonies, presentation and 'movie' modes, morning cues
findings.detail: Demi (4.85 stars, 322 ratings in about 5 months): 'MAGIC PULL… Whisper your wish, tap the orb… subtle haptics, paced breath, a moment of stillness. One wish a day', 'warm paper-grain aesthetic… gentle motion'. Myla 2.0: 'A ritual, not a checklist' breathing orb, plus selectable themes ('Original, After Hours, Grove'). Vision Board ++ (4.85 stars, 3,065 ratings): 'Manifestation Movies', with reviews praising 'visualize, feel, hear your voice'. Vision Board Perfectly Happy (4.83 stars, 4,604 ratings) plays boards as a video slideshow, though some users say it is 'slides… not the vision board people wanted'. Vision Board: Dream & Manifest has a presentation mode with per-board music. Innertune has a morning 'Wake up with positive affirmations' alarm. I am offers custom app icons and themes. Gratitude has 'Gratitude Challenges' and was 'App of the Day'. Stella's emotional peak is the first story, which reviewers say made them cry within an hour.
findings.evidence: Demi lookup (id6763245058); Myla listing https://apps.apple.com/us/app/-/id1638650650 (2.0 notes, screenshots); Vision Board ++ screenshots and reviews (id1609921022); Perfectly Happy reviews (id1486165358); https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6757963805; Innertune and Gratitude screenshots; Stella 5-star reviews 2026-08-01 and 2026-10-01.
findings.implication_for_vela: Give the loop its own ceremonies. 'Seal the proof': press and hold to set a new star into your constellation, with haptics and a soft chime. 'Enter chapter': a dim-and-breathe opening before narration. A weekly 'Arc replay' film: chapter lines, board photos and new stars with an ambient score, rendered on the device. A morning bridge cue notification. A few owned night themes (for example 'Ink', 'Aurora', 'Dawn'). Plan the first-chapter moment as the emotional peak.

findings.title: Pricing benchmarks: Vela's simple, low price is good for ratings; credits, weekly plans and trial billing cause 1-star reviews
findings.detail: Well-rated apps with gentle pricing: Soul ($4.99/month, $19.99–29.99/year; 4.84 stars, 3,744 ratings), Gratitude ($4.99/month, $29.99/year; 4.88 stars, 44,969 ratings), Calyn ($5.99/month, $39.99/year), Vision Board ++ ($4.99/month, $18.99–29.99/year; 4.85 stars). Aggressive pricing: I am (up to $149.99 lifetime, $59.99/year), Innertune (weekly to lifetime, plus a $100 'deep dive' add-on that drew complaints), Moonly ($19.99 add-ons on top of unlimited: 'Everything is still behind a pay wall'). Trial-billing anger shows up everywhere: I am ('you only get 2 days and in the third day it automatically signs you up'), Innertune ('Won't let me cancel'), Myla ('Charged my card before an Alleged 3 Day Free Trial'), Perfectly Happy ('Trial is a trap'). Vela Plus is $4.99/month, $29.99/year and $69.99 lifetime, with no weekly plan.
findings.evidence: IAP sections scraped from apps.apple.com for Soul, Gratitude, Calyn, Vision Board ++, Aya, Future You, Magnetic; I am IAP list (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/874656917); low-star reviews from the RSS feeds for I am, Innertune, Myla, Perfectly Happy and Moonly.
findings.implication_for_vela: Keep pricing as it is: no weekly plan, no credits, no add-ons. Say so on the paywall and in a screenshot ('No weekly plans. No credits. Lifetime available.'). If Vela ever offers a trial, show the end date and remind before billing, since that is a top 1-star trigger in the category.

findings.title: Lost data and unreliable notifications are top-tier trust killers for on-device journaling apps
findings.detail: Gratitude: 'I updated the app and now all of my entries are gone… 2+ years', plus apps that 'force me to buy a plan to restore data'. Innertune: 'new version results in loss of personal data', 'Doesn't sync across devices'. A third-party blog says The Manifest App users report lost journal entries and streak resets. I am: phantom alarms ('alarmed at 2:56am everyday'; 'I have a phantom alarm… I'll have to factory reset my phone'), widgets refreshing 'dozens of times' despite settings, notifications that won't stop on Apple Watch, and a large 'I am' watermark covering affirmations ('Ditch the watermark'). Myla: reminders stopped arriving.
findings.evidence: Gratitude reviews 2026-09-05 and 2026-04-21; Innertune reviews 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-23; I am reviews 2026-05-07, 2026-05-12, 2026-09-17, 2026-09-28, 2026-09-29, 2026-10-13 (RSS feeds); Myla review 2026-01-21; https://www.loa-lawofattraction.co/blog/best-free-manifestation-apps-2026 (biased source: it is published by a competing app).
findings.implication_for_vela: Since everything lives in AsyncStorage, add a private export/backup (a file export or the user's own iCloud Documents, still zero server cost) and a printable 'My Future Memory book' export, and treat data migrations as release-blocking. Keep reminders precise, with one place to turn them off, and never overlay branding on user content.

findings.title: Status of the named incumbents
findings.detail: Shine is gone: Headspace Health bought it in September 2022 and it was removed from both app stores by April 2023, so it needs no benchmark. 'Manifest: Daily Affirmations' is ambiguous. The meaningful app is 'Manifest: Affirmations Daily' by Transcend Labs (4.75 stars, 2,684 ratings): a star-mascot AI chat, mood tracker and challenges companion that moved features behind a paywall and drew 'used to be way better' reviews; Bustle (Nov 2024) rated it 4/5 for its 'vent' feature. A separate 'Manifest - Daily Affirmations' (ZipoApps, 121 ratings) is a basic affirmation app. 'Motivation - Daily quotes' and 'I am' (both by Monkey Taps, 1.07M and 735K ratings) are widget-and-quote apps with no manifestation loop. Moonly (4.64 stars, 31K ratings) is the main moon-ritual app; its 1–2 star share is 63% of recent reviews, driven by paywalls and AI complaints. In vision boards, the leaders are Vision Board Perfectly Happy (4.83 stars, 4.6K ratings), Vision Board & Goal Tracker (4.73, 3.8K), Vision Board ++ (4.85, 3.1K) and Vision Board 2027 (4.58, 2.7K). Myla (4.79, 731 ratings) is the best-designed combined manifest-plus-board app.
findings.evidence: Mozilla Privacy Not Included on Shine https://www.mozillafoundation.org/en/privacynotincluded/shine; iTunes Search API results (Oct 15, 2026); Bustle review https://www.bustle.com/wellness/manifestation-app-review-features; https://apps.apple.com/us/app/manifest-daily-affirmations/id1631748635; Moonly review-feed distribution.
findings.implication_for_vela: Benchmark against Stella, Aya, Future You and Magnetic (AI stories), I am and Motivation (widgets and retention), and Myla and Vision Board ++ (visual polish and boards), not Shine. The empty space is 'manifestation that asks you to act and remembers what you did'.

recommendations: 1. Rebuild the App Store screenshots around the loop and the free/private promise, roughly in this order: (1) a chapter page over its own generative night sky, headline like 'A story about your future, written on your phone'; (2) 'One small bridge to reality' (the bridge card); (3) 'Log what actually happened' (proof check-in); (4) 'Tomorrow's chapter remembers' (chapter 2 quoting the proof, highlighted); (5) 'Watch your constellation grow' (a rich star map); (6) widgets; (7) 'Unlimited listens. No account. No weekly plans.' Leave out laurels, '#1', testimonials, photos of people, the phrase 'future self', pink, and black-and-gold slides that resemble Magnetic.

2. Build an on-device generative art system (react-native-svg or Skia, seeded by dream ID): a distinct sky or chapter plate per dream, where the stars are the user's logged proofs. This adds visual richness without AI images or photos of people, avoiding the diversity and 'AI slop' backlash Stella and Moonly get.

3. Upgrade the chapter player: background audio with lock-screen controls, sleep timer, loop, 'play my arc', a Short (about 3 minutes) or Deep (6–8 minutes) length choice, original ambient beds, a voice picker that prefers enhanced/premium system voices, a 'how to say my name' field, optional people and pronouns, no auto-advance, and tap-to-edit a line with the engine remembering the edit.

4. Ship iOS widgets that serve the loop: 'Today's bridge' (tap to log proof), 'Constellation', and a lock-screen line widget. Widgets drove the 1M-rating incumbents, and no competitor has an action-and-proof widget.

5. Deepen the proof constellation as the hero: a per-dream star map with tappable stars (the proof sentence plus the chapter line it changed), a press-and-hold 'Seal the proof' ceremony with haptics, a weekly or monthly 'Arc replay' put together on the device, 'On this day' resurfacing, and designed share images of the constellation. Avoid 'proof wall/board' and 'signs/synchronicity' wording.

6. Link the Board to chapters: pinned photos become scene anchors in the next chapter and can be attached as proof photos; add a presentation mode with ambient sound. Reconsider the 3-card free cap (one or two free boards is a frequent 1-star complaint for vision-board apps), for example by making the board part of the one free dream.

7. Add on-device own-voice recording (expo-audio) for the bridge sentence or a favourite chapter line, played as a morning cue. Don't use voice cloning or Apple's Personal Voice API (Apple frames Personal Voice as mainly for assistive-communication apps).
8. Make the streak forgiving: show 'nights in your arc' with grace days, and never shame a reset to zero. Losing a streak is a proven 1-star trigger (I am, Gratitude).

9. Protect trust: keep onboarding at 6 steps or fewer with an explicit 'nothing leaves this phone' line; promise that everything a user made stays readable if Plus lapses; add a private export/backup (file or the user's own iCloud) and a 'Future Memory book' export; keep reminders precise and easy to switch off.

10. Keep pricing simple ($4.99/month, $29.99/year, $69.99 lifetime; no weekly plans, credits or add-ons) and say so on the paywall and in screenshots. Pricing is the category's top complaint and Vela's clearest edge over Stella ($6.99/week), Aya ($9.99/week plus per-audio fees) and Daya ($7.99/week).

11. Stay out of the crowded zones for 4.3 safety: no specific-person or ex-recovery goals, no subliminals or frequencies, no tarot, moon or astrology, no AI chat coach, no swipe affirmation deck or 369 as the hero, no 'meet your future self' photo swipes. Keep affirmations, 369, script and gratitude as supporting rituals that feed the action-and-proof loop.

research.summary: Across the apps I looked at, the evidence for daily opens is strongest for surfaces that sit outside the app and show the user's own living state. The best example is home-screen and lock-screen widgets: Gratitude reported 25% higher retention among widget users. After iOS 14 widgets, DAU of the I am and Motivation apps rose 100% while Calm and Headspace stalled. Duolingo found that widget users stay active longer even after allowing for the fact that they were already more engaged. Finch's widget pet comes with D1/D7 retention of 54%/37%. Next come forgiving progress mechanics (Duolingo's Weekend Amulet test: +4% returned a week later; Apple's pause rings; Finch pets that cannot die). Then personal, well-timed reminders (Calm's reminder prompt: 40% opted in, and retention rose by the same amount seen in users who had found the setting themselves; Duolingo's rotating notification templates: +2% new-user retention). After those: a collectible growth metaphor (Opal has had 2M+ gem reveals; the endowed-progress study saw 34% vs 19% completion), recaps timed to "fresh start" dates, and Wrapped-style identity cards, which work more for acquisition than retention. Vela has almost none of this today. It has no widget and no Live Activity. Notifications are one or two fixed daily repeats with the same copy forever (lib/notifications.ts), including "the streak stays lit". Progress is a classic consecutive-day streak that resets to 0 (lib/streak.ts). The "constellation" is a row of 7 dots. There are no recaps, no share cards except on affirmations, and "Listen" is plain text-to-speech with no sound bed. Every mechanic below can be built with zero servers. expo-widgets has been stable since SDK 56, and Vela is on SDK 57, so widgets, interactive buttons on iOS 17+, timelines and locally started Live Activities need no backend. Local notifications can be rebuilt as a rolling queue under iOS's 64-pending cap. Ambient sound can be generated on the device, so it is original and has no licensing cost. Recaps and cards can be computed and rendered locally. The research also gives Vela a defensible core: pure positive fantasy lowers effort (Oettingen), while rehearsing the steps plus if-then plans improves goal attainment (MCII g=0.34, implementation intentions d=0.65). That is exactly Vela's bridge-and-proof loop. So expansion should make that loop visible everywhere (sky, widget, lock screen, recap, card) rather than add generic quote or affirmation surfaces, which would revive the 4.3 'too similar' risk. Most evidence is correlational or self-reported by companies or vendors; I mark this where it applies.

findings.title: Home-screen and lock-screen widgets show the best evidence for driving daily opens, and Vela has none
findings.detail: Gratitude (Android Developers Blog, May 2026): widgets showing journaling prompts, affirmations, vision-board images and metrics gave 25% higher retention among widget users. 10% of DAU adopted them. Installs were driven by in-app prompts to pin the widget at relevant moments. Monkey Taps (I am / Motivation) shipped widgets on iOS 14 launch day. Apptopia reports Affirmation/Motivation DAU up 100% from August 2020, while the two leading meditation apps stagnated through 2021. Duolingo says widget users stay active longer 'even after accounting for' already being more engaged, and half of widget installers have 6+ month streaks. Installs rose 'drastically' once an animated install guide appeared after a lesson. User research found a simple is-it-at-risk state beat extra stats. Duo's mood changes with time of day and completion state. Finch's widget is a living pet that shows 'adventure in progress' and 'completed' states and changes with seasons. Sensor Tower estimates via Deconstructor of Fun put Finch at ~10M MAU and D1/D7 54%/37% (Duolingo 51/35). Locket shows a widget can be the whole product (#1 App Store in 30+ countries). Caveat: all of this is correlational or company-reported, except Duolingo's stated adjustment.

This is feasible with zero servers. expo-widgets is stable since SDK 56 and supports systemSmall/Medium/Large plus lock-screen accessoryCircular, accessoryRectangular and accessoryInline. It shares data through an App Group directory. Dated timeline entries (updateTimeline) let the widget change through the day without the app running. Buttons are interactive on iOS 17+. Widget code runs in an isolated runtime with @expo/ui/swift-ui components only, so no hooks or async. Proposed set:
- Small 'Tonight's line': one sentence from the current chapter in serif on night sky, deep-linking into the chapter.
- Medium 'Today's bridge': the bridge text plus an 'I crossed it' button that opens proof capture prefilled. The one-sentence proof stays in-app so the loop stays honest.

- Lock screen: rectangular shows the bridge; circular shows arc stars (e.g. 3/9); inline reads 'Chapter 3 is waiting'.
The widget shifts by time of day: morning shows the bridge, after proof it shows 'Chapter 3 begins from what happened', evening shows the chapter line.
When the app opens, write the next 7 days of timeline entries. Ask users to add the widget on the proof-success screen, with an animated guide (iOS cannot pin widgets programmatically).
Guardrail: the widget shows only the user's own desire, chapter, bridge and proof. A rotating generic quote is exactly the I am / Motivation pattern and invites another 4.3. Verify in a dev build how a widget button tap gets back to the app, since addUserInteractionListener only fires while the app is alive. Widgets on home and lock screens also make App Store screenshots far more striking.

findings.title: Replace the consecutive-day streak with forgiving, cumulative progress
findings.detail: Duolingo's Weekend Amulet A/B test (keep the streak through the weekend without using the app): offered learners were 4% more likely to return a week later and 5% less likely to lose their streak. Weekend DAU dips 5-10%. Separating the streak from the daily goal, so the smallest unit counts: D14 retention +3.3%, DAU +1%, learners on a streak +10.5%. A year later, just over half of daily learners had 7+ day streaks, up from about a third. Retention is most fragile in the first 7 days. Apple's watchOS 11 'Pause Rings' lets users pause up to ~90 days without losing a streak. Headspace lets members hide streaks (tagged loss aversion and anxiety). Finch's FAQ says pets cannot die because it 'could be too anxiety-inducing'. A Lund University researcher warns that urgent framing in stress apps raises anxiety. Calm community members switch streaks off because they stress them out.

Vela's evidence screen is literally headed 'PROOF, NOT PRESSURE'. Yet its progress model and notification copy rest on loss aversion. That contradicts the Future Memory idea that proof piles up and never expires. Changes:

findings.title: Personal, event-driven local notifications instead of one fixed daily repeat
findings.detail: Calm (Amplitude case study): the daily reminder was buried in Settings and fewer than 1% found it. Those users retained ~3x better. Prompting new users to set a reminder right after their first session got 40% to opt in, and retention rose by the same amount. Duolingo (KDD 2020 'Sleeping, Recovering Bandit'): rotating notification templates while modelling novelty decay gave +0.5% DAU and +2% new-user retention over an already strong baseline. Co-Star: the daily notification is effectively the product, and blunt, personal lines get screenshotted and shared. Opt-in permission is scarce: OneSignal reports 33.5% iOS opt-in for Health & Fitness in 2024. Fabulous designs reminders as cues for a specific ritual, not nags. iOS keeps only the 64 soonest pending local notifications per app; a repeating request counts as one.

findings.implication_for_vela:
On every app open or foreground, rebuild a rolling 7-14 day queue of one-off local notifications, keeping under 64 pending. Copy comes from the user's own data, for example:
- 'Yesterday you wrote: "Sent my portfolio to two studios." Chapter 3 begins there.'
- 'Your bridge for today: create one visible piece of work.'
Event triggers:
- chapter ready the morning after a proof
- a bridge check-in at the user's if-then time
- time-capsule unlocks
- new month / new moon fresh starts
Rotate 20-40 templates per slot. Run a tiny on-device bandit: record which notification opened the app via the response listener (stored locally only) and down-weight stale templates. Move the permission ask to after the first chapter or proof ('Want tomorrow's chapter to find you?'), the Calm pattern. Never use guilt or loss copy.

findings.title: Make the constellation a real, growing collection with reveal moments
findings.detail: Finch's growth loop: self-care tasks give energy, the pet evolves and goes on timed adventures, and the widget and seasons update. Estimated D1/D7 is 54%/37%. Opal's 'MileStone' gem has been revealed by 2M+ people. It is a crafted 3D reveal with particles, reward sound and haptics, and the gem grows brighter as focus improves. Endowed-progress effect (Nunes & Dreze 2006): a 10-stamp card with 2 pre-stamped reached 34% completion vs 19% for an empty 8-stamp card, with the same effort required. Goal-gradient (Kivetz et al. 2006): people speed up as they near a goal, and stronger acceleration predicts retention. The design skill's own conventions: make the 'peak' a personalized insight moment, and make milestone celebrations proportional.

Each arc becomes a constellation drawn in react-native-svg:
- Every proof is a star, with colour and brightness by type: I did it = gold, I moved = white, I learned = blue.
- Lines join proofs in order.
- Tapping a star reads back the user's proof sentence.
Arc completion triggers a reveal ceremony (Reanimated plus haptics): the user names the constellation, which is then 'set' into Your Sky. Your Sky is a persistent, pannable night sky of every completed arc across focus areas. This is the collectible that Finch's bird and Opal's gem provide, but it is made of the user's real-world proof, so it is unique to Vela and strengthens the 4.3 case.
Endowed progress: naming the desire lights star 1 and listening to Chapter 1 lights star 2 of 9, instead of starting at 0 of 7. Stars never dim or disappear (the Finch rule). The same sky feeds the large widget, recaps and share cards.

findings.title: A guided 'threshold' session that turns visualization into rehearsal, with evidence behind it
findings.detail: Oettingen's research: indulging only in positive fantasies of the outcome lowers energy and later effort and achievement. Mental contrasting with implementation intentions (MCII): meta-analysis of 21 studies and 15,907 participants, g = 0.336 for goal attainment. Implementation intentions alone: d = 0.65 across 94 tests (Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006). Effects are larger for if-then plans that are rehearsed. Taylor & Pham (1999): students who mentally simulated the process (studying) rather than the outcome (getting the grade) studied more and got better grades, through better planning and lower anxiety. Breathwork RCT meta-analysis (Fincham et al. 2023): g = -0.35 on self-reported stress, with moderate risk of bias.

Vela's bridge already separates it from outcome-fantasy apps like Stella. Make that visible and guided with a 2-3 minute session, all on-device:
1. 30-60 seconds of paced breathing with an expanding star ring.
2. The chapter.
3. 'Rehearse the bridge' (45 seconds): see where you are, when it is, and your first move.
4. Optionally, one obstacle line plus an if-then ('If it's 9am and I hesitate, then I open the portfolio file').
The if-then time then drives the bridge notification, widget and Live Activity. This is the evidence-backed answer to 'manifestation is wishful thinking'. It is strong material for App Review notes and listing copy. Avoid medical or health claims.

findings.title: Night is the prime-time slot: ambient sound beds and a 'sleep chapter' mode
findings.detail: Headspace 2025 Year in Review: busiest hours were 9-11pm. Most-played sound genres were soundscapes, sleep music, focus music, wind-downs and sleepcasts. 'Brown Noise' was the favourite in three of four US regions and in the UK. Calm's Sleep Stories began when staff saw a night-time usage spike; ~300 stories have been played more than 450 million times. Harvey & Payne (2002): insomniacs who pictured a calm scene fell asleep more than 20 minutes sooner; counting sheep did not help. A Stella App Store review asks for read-aloud affirmations and custom voice narration. Apple says the Personal Voice API is meant mainly for augmentative and alternative communication apps, a risk for App Review.

findings.title: Recaps on fresh-start dates (weekly ledger, monthly sky, Year of Proof)
findings.detail: Fresh-start effect (Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014): searches for 'diet', gym visits and goal commitments all rise after temporal landmarks such as a new week, month or year. Headspace's busiest day of 2025 was the first Monday of January. How We Feel runs a weekly review every Sunday, unlocked after at least 3 check-ins. Opal's weekly Focus Report unlocks after a full week. Daylio's Year in Pixels is valued for looking back; users keep logging so they don't 'lose' memories (qualitative). Duolingo reports lessons and time spent went up after users went through Year in Review. Strava put Year in Sport behind its $80 subscription in 2025 and drew a loud backlash. Day One's 'On This Day' is called 'a great motivator to journal' (anecdotal).

All computed locally from the proof log:
- Sunday 'Proof Ledger': bridges crossed, the did/moved/learned mix, the sentence of the week, which desire moved, and next week's first bridge. Only shown after 2+ proofs, so it never displays emptiness.
- Monthly 'Night Sky' on the 1st: the month's constellations, a 'what became real' timeline, and a fresh-start prompt to renew or sharpen the desire.
- 'Year of Proof' in December: a Wrapped-style story.
Keep the core recaps free, given Strava's backlash. Plus can add deeper patterns, such as which bridge types you finish fastest or what time of day you act. Recaps also give natural notification moments.

findings.detail: FutureMe (letters to your future self) lists 8M+ users. Most people schedule delivery within about three years, and 30 days is the minimum. Day One users describe daily 'On This Day' reminders as 'eye-opening' and a motivator to keep writing (anecdotal). Daylio users keep logging partly so they don't 'lose' memories.

findings.title: Share cards should express identity, not report app usage
findings.detail: Spotify Wrapped 2025 reached 200M engaged users and 500M shares in about 24 hours (+41% shares year on year). Duolingo Year in Review: comparison stats lifted share rates, the top 10% of XP earners made over half of all shares in 2020, and personality-style 'learner styles' were a second share hook that 'significantly boosted share rates'. Co-Star's acquisition came largely from users screenshotting personal notifications. The design skill's 'Vanity Mirror' principle: celebrate who users are, not what they did in the app.

- Proof-star card: the user's own proof sentence typeset as a star. Hide the desire by default, since the content is intimate.
- Constellation-complete card.
- Monthly or yearly 'manifester archetype': local rules, e.g. 'The Quiet Builder' when most proofs are 'I moved', 'The Student of Signs' for 'I learned'.
- Then-vs-now time-capsule card.
With no server there are no cross-user comparisons, so use self-comparisons ('your fastest bridge'). Add a small Vela mark. This is mainly a free acquisition loop, and it also produces strong listing visuals.

findings.detail: OneSignal says apps using Live Activities have 23.7% higher average 30-day retention. That is vendor data and correlational. Structured (2026 Apple Design Award finalist) and Opal use Live Activities and interactive widgets for timed sessions, and Structured includes them in its free tier. Platform limits: up to 8 hours active, and at most 12 hours on the Lock Screen. expo-widgets' createLiveActivity can start, update and end activities locally; push is optional.

findings.implication_for_vela: When the user commits to a bridge window (from the if-then step, e.g. 'today before 6pm'), start a local Live Activity. The Lock Screen shows the bridge sentence, time left and arc stars; the compact Dynamic Island shows a star glyph. It ends on proof, or at the window's end with a soft dismissal. Make it opt-in, with a calm tone and no countdown-shaming. Chapter playback already gets the system Now Playing controls, so no Live Activity is needed there. The evidence is weaker than for widgets, so build this after them.

findings.detail: The fresh-start effect (above) explains why new weeks, months, years and other landmarks restart goal pursuit. Moon-phase utilities have millions of estimated installs. But manifestation-specific moon apps (Moonifest, Moonly) have only dozens to low hundreds of ratings. That suggests the moon works as a feature or cadence, not a standalone product. Finch refreshes its widget with the seasons. Headspace's peak day is the first Monday of January.

- New moon: name or renew a desire (a fresh start).

findings.title: How to measure and showcase it without an analytics SDK
findings.detail: Health & Fitness retention benchmarks vary with the definition used: D30 is ~3% in Sendbird's medians and ~8% in Unstar's. AppsFlyer 2025 reports Health & Fitness among the biggest year-on-year retention gainers (+22%). Finch's estimated 54/37 D1/D7 is top tier. Apple's featuring criteria include Innovation ('new technologies'), Uniqueness, Accessibility, Localization and 'compelling screenshots'. Apple asks for at least 2 weeks' notice and recommends nominating up to 3 months ahead in App Store Connect.

It covers users who opt in to share with developers, and I believe it includes retention cohorts; verify in the console. Ship features in separate versions so cohorts can be compared. Pair the widget / Live Activity / sky release with a Featuring Nomination. Rebuild the screenshot set around the most striking surfaces: lock screen with bridge and stars, home-screen widgets, Your Sky reveal, sleep player and recap card. This answers the owner's 'screenshots' ask.

recommendations: Ship a 'Living Sky' release next, before the 1 January 2027 fresh-start peak. It has four parts: (1) forgiving, cumulative progress that never resets, with weekly rhythm, automatic rest nights and a pause; (2) the constellation rebuilt as a collectible sky with a reveal ceremony and endowed progress (start at 2 of 9 stars); (3) expo-widgets: small chapter line, medium bridge with an 'I crossed it' button, large sky, plus lock-screen rectangular and circular; (4) a rolling 7-14 day queue of local notifications written from the user's own chapter, bridge and proof sentences. Everything is on-device and needs no new backend.

Pre-write a week of dated widget timeline entries whenever the app opens so it changes through the day without the app running.

Second release, 'Night Ritual':
- A guided threshold session: breath, chapter, 45 seconds rehearsing the bridge, then an if-then plan (MCII g=0.34; implementation intentions d=0.65; process simulation beats outcome simulation).
- Ambient beds generated on the device with react-native-audio-api: brown noise, rain, drone. Original, no licensing.
- A 'sleep chapter' mode with timer and fade.

- An opt-in Live Activity for the committed bridge window.
Avoid the Personal Voice API.

Third release, 'Proof Ledger', live by early December 2026:

- A monthly Night Sky on the 1st.

Monetization split: keep the retention drivers free (one widget set, the sky, core recaps, one ambient bed, forgiving progress). Put extras behind Plus: more arcs and skies, extra beds and sleep-chapter lengths, more widget styles and sky themes, deeper pattern insights, and extra time-capsule slots.

Measure without an SDK: stage the releases as separate versions and compare App Store Connect retention cohorts (opt-in users; confirm the exact metrics in the console). Rebuild the App Store screenshots around the lock screen with bridge and stars, home-screen widgets, the sky reveal, the sleep player and a recap card.

research.summary: Vela's live listing is the weakest part of its funnel. The iTunes lookup API for id 6797328581 (fetched 2026-10-15) returns only 3 screenshots, 0 ratings, the name "Vela: Manifestation Journal" (not "Manifestation Stories"), subtitle "Future Self Visualization" and category Lifestyle. Among the 12 category leaders I pulled, sets run 5 to 10 frames (median about 8.5). Stella uses 5. The 3 live frames also have production defects. The phone UI is cropped on the right, so sentences run off the screen. It was captured at 381x825 and upscaled about 2.6x, so it looks soft. Frame 3 shows a gold CTA button with no label and the line "1 moments have shaped your arc". The eyebrow, subline and pill text (22-34px on a 1290 canvas) shrink to about 2-3pt in the 3-up search row, so they can't be read. Apple's own pages confirm the first 1-3 portrait frames are what search shows when there is no app preview. Older but consistent data from SplitMetrics (about 1,800 tests) and AppAgent/Phiture says only 9-15% of visitors swipe deep into a set. So frames 1-3 have to explain Vela's loop on their own. Competitor teardown: incumbents lead with social proof (Calm, Stella, Rise, Day One, Stoic), short 2-4-word benefit headlines, real device frames with UI pieces popping out of the frame, and a "peak" state (Finch's streak, Rise's numbers). Journal apps use a privacy frame. Vela has no ratings, so its proof has to come from the product's unique mechanic instead. The recommended 1.1 set has 9 frames plus an optional 10th. Frames 1-3 form a search-visible triptych: story, then one real step, then your proof writes chapter two. These are joined by a gold "constellation thread" and followed by a full-bleed proof-constellation peak frame. The supporting rituals sit at the back, which also keeps the 4.3 "distinctive loop" positioning App Review accepted. Several frames depend on 1.1 visuals that don't exist yet (a real constellation sky, a narration player with line highlighting). Under guidelines 2.3.1 and 2.3.3 they can only ship once those features are in the binary, so a fallback screen is given for each.

findings.title: Caption sizes are unreadable in search results, where the first 3 frames do most of the work
findings.detail: Apple: "Depending on the orientation of your screenshots, the first one to three images will appear in search results when no app preview is available, so make sure these highlight the essence of your app." In a 3-up search row each portrait frame is roughly 115-130pt wide on a 402-440pt-wide iPhone (my estimate), so 1 canvas px is about 0.09-0.1pt. On that scale, Vela's 92px Georgia headline is about 9pt, the 34px subline about 3pt, the 28px letter-spaced eyebrow ("VELA · FUTURE MEMORY STUDIO") about 2.7pt, and the 22px pill about 2pt. Phiture/AppAgent (2017, about 25k visitors) advises one-liners of about 4 words that are readable without enlarging.

findings.title: Few visitors swipe deep, so frames 1-3 must explain the loop by themselves
findings.detail: SplitMetrics (2018, about 1,800 A/B tests): only 11% of users reached the 5th portrait screenshot (15% for landscape). Optimized screenshots averaged about an 18% conversion lift, with case lifts of 25.6% (SEGA caption storytelling) and 45% (OLBG zoomed UI elements). Phiture/AppAgent (2017): 9% scroll portrait screenshots, under 4% enlarge them, and under 1% expand the description. The average decision takes about 7 seconds. Secondhand Storemaven data (500M+ users) agrees: everyone sees the first-impression frames, and only "explorers" go further. These figures are old and vendor-sourced, but they all point the same way.

findings.title: Apple spec and rule facts that constrain the set (verified 2026-10-15)
findings.detail: The live App Store Connect spec page lists the required iPhone size as "At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)": 1206x2622 or 1179x2556 (iPhone 17/17 Pro/18 Pro). The large Dynamic Island size (iPhone 17 Pro Max/Air) accepts 1320x2868, 1290x2796 or 1260x2736. The 6.5-inch size (1284x2778 / 1242x2688) is "Required if app runs on iPhone and screenshots for iPhone with Dynamic Island (large display) aren't provided". Other facts: up to 10 per size, jpg/png, no alpha. New this year: iPhone Duo sizes (outer 1398x2034, inner 2007x2853) become required in April 2027 for apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later. Review rules: 2.3.3 says screenshots must "show the app in use", and text and image overlays are allowed. 2.3.7 says screenshots "should not include prices" and subtitles must not "reference other apps, or make unverifiable product claims". 2.3.1 forbids promoting features the app doesn't offer. 5.2.4 forbids implying Apple endorsement; Editor's Choice badges are applied by Apple. Apple also says: "If your app supports Dark Mode, consider including at least one screenshot".

findings.title: Competitor teardown: what the winning sets do
findings.detail: Stella (5 frames, 5,346 ratings): pink-lilac pastel gradient, heavy sans headlines in dark plum, real iPhone frames. Its order is: (1) "#1 Manifestation App" laurel over a personalized home ("Sarah, what do you want to manifest?"); (2) "Join 300,000+ others." with three 5-star review cards and avatars; (3) "Personalized visualizations.", a tilted phone with a full-bleed photo and one story line; (4) "Meet your future self." with photo story cards; (5) "Daily affirmations." Calm opens with logo + "#1 App for Sleep & Meditation" + "3M 5-Star Reviews" + App Store Awards laurels, then press logos and Editor's Choice, then content with celebrity faces and tilted, overlapping devices. Headspace uses a strong brand color, two-tone headlines (keyword in orange: "Stress less", "Sleep soundly") and cards that pop out of the device. Rise is the closest palette analog to Vela: dark purple night fading to a sunset horizon, "Become a morning person" + "Trusted by 5 million" + press logos, and big data callouts ("6.3 hrs Sleep debt", "Peak", "Dip") that break out of the frame. Finch opens with character art and no device, uses chunky 3-line headlines, and shows a celebratory "30 DAY STREAK" peak. Stoic is monochrome editorial with App of the Day / Editors' Choice laurels, "Join 4 million+" with a review card, and a passcode privacy frame last. Day One puts "100% Private" at frame 2. I am, Soul, Mantra, Gratitude, Stoic and Rise all include lock-screen or widget frames. Soul (6 frames) uses purple cosmic starfields with glowing device outlines and lavender uppercase keyword emphasis, which is visually the nearest neighbor to Vela's indigo night. Shine is no longer findable on the US App Store, so it couldn't be analyzed.

findings.detail: Vela has 0 ratings, so a rating laurel, user count or review card would be fabricated. That breaks guideline 2.3.1 and the Section 3 rules on review manipulation. Verifiable claims it does have: App Privacy "Data Not Collected" (checklist), no account, on-device generation, offline narration, and no daily listening limit on your story (the free tier allows unlimited listens). Stella's own description stresses server-generated personalized audio. The "no daily limit" claim contrasts with competitors without naming one, which 2.3.7 forbids. AppTweak also advises against promotional text like "Free" in screenshots.

findings.title: Device frames vs full-bleed, panoramic sets and caption-text indexing: weak evidence, so treat them as test variables
findings.detail: No published controlled test isolates framed vs full-bleed, or panoramic vs single frames. The often-quoted "30% lift" for panoramas is untraceable vendor marketing. A secondhand figure says only about 11% scroll a full panorama. Appfigures claims Apple has extracted "some" screenshot text as ranking keywords since about June 2025. A ConsultMyApp test of 64 caption phrases found "no strong evidence", and Apple hasn't confirmed it. Better documented: since July 2025, keywords can be assigned to Custom Product Pages for organic search (limit raised to 70 pages, Oct 2025, per several ASO vendors). Apple's Product Page Optimization runs up to 3 treatments for up to 90 days, with screenshot-only tests submitted independently of an app version.

recommendations: GLOBAL SYSTEM. Master canvas 1320x2868, also exported to 1206x2622 (Apple's listed required medium size), both uploaded. Background: a 'Vela night' gradient, #0E0C22 at the top through #1E1840 to #3A2A4F, with a warm gold horizon bloom (#E9B44C at about 18%, radial, lower third) and a sparse star field, so thumbnails read as dusk rather than black tiles. Shift each frame slightly warmer from 1 to 9 (night becoming dawn: the future becoming real). Headlines: one OFL serif at weight 600 (e.g., Newsreader or Fraunces, echoing the in-app Georgia story type), 136-150px, ivory #F6EFE3, one keyword in gold #E9B44C, at most 2 lines and 5 words per line, top-left anchored. Sublines: sans 52-56px at 70% ivory, at most 2 lines. No eyebrows, no pills under 40px. Real iPhone 17 Pro bezel from Apple Design Resources, 9:41 status bar, device bleeding off the bottom about 8% so the UI is bigger. In every frame, lift one hero UI component 1.2-1.3x out of the device with a gold-tinted soft glow (never a gray or black shadow). Copy bans: prices, 'free', '#1', ratings or user counts, competitor names, health or outcome guarantees. Use en-US spelling.

FRAME 1 (search triptych, part 1 of 3: the story). Screen/state: story reader in a new 1.1 'narrating' state. Chapter title 'The Day the Dream Went Ordinary', the current sentence highlighted in gold, a mini player 'Listening · Chapter 1', and the user's own words visible in the text. Headline: 'Your future, written as a *story*.' Subline: 'A personal manifestation chapter from your own words, read aloud on your iPhone.' Treatment: centered device. Pop-out chip at top-left in quotes: "my own design studio, with clients who trust my eye", joined by a thin gold constellation thread to the highlighted sentence. The thread exits the right edge into frame 2. Fallback if line highlighting doesn't ship: current reader (screen 10) captured at 3x with the gold quote chip as overlay.

FRAME 2 (triptych, part 2: the bridge). Screen/state: end of chapter showing the 'Bridge to reality' card ('Create one visible piece of work, however small, before consuming advice.') with 'Make it observable'. Headline: 'Then take one *real* step.' Subline: 'Every chapter ends with one small, observable action for today.' Treatment: device offset right. The bridge card is popped out 1.25x toward the left with the footsteps icon and a star node on the gold thread that came in from frame 1 and exits to frame 3.

FRAME 3 (triptych, part 3: the unique mechanic, which is also the one App Review verified for 4.3). Screen/state: chapter 2 in the reader with the proof sentence woven into the story and highlighted ('There is proof behind this memory now: I sent my portfolio to two studios I admire.'), tagged 'Woven from your proof'. Headline: 'What you did writes *chapter two*.' Subline: 'Log one honest sentence. Vela weaves it into tomorrow's story.' Treatment: device centered. A popped-out proof card ('I did it · Sent my portfolio to two studios I admire.') with a gold line flowing into the highlighted sentence, so the triptych ends on the payoff.

FRAME 4 (the peak, full-bleed with no device; the set's visual signature). Screen/state: a new 1.1 full-screen proof constellation sky with 6-9 gold stars joined by lines. One star is tapped and shows 'Day 3 · I moved · Sent my portfolio…'. Headline: 'Every step becomes a *star*.' Subline: 'Your proof constellation grows with each arc. No scores, no streak shame.' Treatment: the frameless screenshot fills the canvas under the headline, like Finch and I am do. This is also the best variant to test against frame 1 in Product Page Optimization. Fallback until it ships: the evidence-success screen 'A point of proof' (screen 16) in a device.

FRAME 5 (the main objection to the incumbent, without naming it). Screen/state: the full narration player (1.1: chapter sky art, scrubber, voice and speed controls) or the current reader with the Listen pill. Headline: 'Listen as often as you *like*.' Subline: 'No daily listening limit on your story. Read or play it anytime, even offline.' Treatment: device tilted 6°. The play control is popped out with a soft gold glow. Don't show lock-screen Now Playing unless 1.1 actually implements it.

FRAME 6 (personalization, a category convention used by Stella and Soul). Screen/state: intake filled. 'Career' selected, words 'my own design studio, with clients who trust my eye', feeling 'proud' selected. Headline: 'Start with what you're *calling in*.' Subline: 'Pick a focus, say it in your words, name the feeling.' Treatment: device offset left. The six focus chips (Love, Abundance, Career, Health, Confidence, Peace) float out of the frame on the right.

FRAME 7 (supporting rituals, deliberately after the loop to keep the 4.3 positioning). Screen/state: two overlapping devices. Front: affirmation card 'The imposter voice retired; the craftsman stayed.' Back: the 3·6·9 journal with a filled line and progress. Headline: 'Rituals that serve your *story*.' Subline: 'Affirmations, 3·6·9, scripting and gratitude, tuned to your focus.'

FRAME 8 (vision board). Screen/state: the board filled with 6 cards (mixed photos and written goals). Use only original or properly licensed images in the seed data. Headline: 'Pin the life you're *building*.' Subline: 'A private vision board that lives beside your proof.' Treatment: centered device, one photo card popped out. research.summary: Vela is a small, clean codebase: about 8.7k lines, 18 route files and 6 React contexts, with no shared component layer at all. Everything lives on the device in AsyncStorage. Today I ran bun test (67 tests pass, 943 expect() calls, 9 files) and `tsc --noEmit` (exit 0). The Future Memory loop is real in code but thin. The engine has 118 original fragments (2,786 words). The arrival and living pools have only 6 fragments per focus area, and there are 10 titles. Each focus area has just 3 bridge actions, picked by hash with no repeat guard: in a 300-step sample, 52 chapter changes repeated the previous action exactly. Proof is added as one paragraph after the story's closing beat, and only the newest proof is used. Each new chapter replaces the old one (no chapter history), and the onboarding "mood" answer is stored but never used. Two things must be fixed before any visual work: (a) the contexts read state from a stale snapshot, so two writes in one handler (for example save proof, then weave the next chapter) will silently lose data; (b) there are no UI primitives, so 15 screens each have their own StyleSheet and the cta/dock/close/header styles are copied up to 10 times. Screens also use 13 font sizes outside the 4-size scale and have 0 accessibilityLabels. The screenshot problem is mostly in the pipeline. The live store shots upscale 381x825 web captures about 2.6x into 1290x2796 frames, and the web build draws text in Times and Segoe UI while iOS uses Georgia and SF. The existing CDP harness can already capture at 430x932 @3x (exactly 1290x2796), and bundled fonts would make web and iOS look the same. On SDK 57 (expo 57.0.9 / expo-modules-core 57.0.8), the safe, high-impact additions are expo-linear-gradient 57.0.1, expo-font plus @expo-google-fonts, expo-audio 57.0.3, react-native-view-shot 5.1.0 and expo-sharing 57.0.8. I tested the audio path: numpy/scipy plus ffmpeg 8.1.2 on PATH produced an original 60-second loop as a 733 KB AAC file. Home-screen widgets are feasible using the Scripture Mate pattern found locally, but they carry the most signing and native-build risk. Skia and Lottie are not worth it for v2. Releases are local EAS builds on free macos-26 GitHub runners (the repo is public). Every push to review-rebuild starts a build, and the build number must be raised by hand from 4.

findings.detail:
Expo Router with 18 route files. Root `app/_layout.tsx` nests 6 providers in this order: User > Story > Ritual > Journal > Plus > Board. It shows a blank bg View until UserContext is ready, then uses `Stack.Protected`: if a profile exists you get (tabs), otherwise onboarding. All screen transitions are `fade` with headers hidden.

- `(tabs)/index` (Today): greeting, streak chip, the Future Memory card for `intents[0]` only, a Bridge card (Record proof) or a Folded card (Weave chapter N+1), a 7-dot proof constellation, and two supporting-ritual cards.
- `(tabs)/stories`: list of intents with their current story; long-press opens Alert to 'release' (delete); + goes to `/story/new`.

findings.title: How the story engine works, and why the loop feels limited
findings.detail:
`composeStory` (lib/story/engine.ts) seeds mulberry32 and picks one fragment for each of 7 beats (opening > arrival > sensory > living > witness > gratitude > closing) plus a title. It avoids fragment ids already in `intent.usedIds` and fills {name}/{desire}/{feeling}/{domain} with split/join. Pool sizes per focus: opening 10, arrival 6, sensory 10, living 6, witness 8, gratitude 8, closing 10, titles 10. So arrival and living start repeating after chapter 6, and titles after chapter 10. A story is about 250 words, which is roughly 1.5 to 2 minutes of narration.

The Future Memory part (lib/futureMemory.ts):
- `deriveFutureAction` = ACTIONS[focus][hash(focus|desire|chapter) % 3]. Only 3 actions per focus and no avoid-set. I measured it over 6 focus areas x 5 desires x 10 chapters (300 chapter steps): 52 chapter changes repeat the previous action exactly.
- `evidenceBridge` produces one fixed sentence ('There is proof behind this memory now: …'). StoryContext.render appends it after the closing beat, and it uses only the most recent evidence. evidenceKind (did/moved/learned) only changes the success-card copy, never the story.
- regenerate() always increments `chapter`, even from the reader's refresh icon with no new proof. It re-weaves the same old proof each time and leaves the previous open action orphaned.
- `stories` keeps one rendering per intent ('the newest rendering replaces the old'), so earlier chapters are deleted. There is no history to show as an arc.
- `profile.mood` is collected in onboarding ('The stories meet you where you are') but nothing reads it.
- Journal entries, 369 phrases and board cards never feed the engine. The supporting rituals are disconnected from the loop.
findings.evidence: lib\story\engine.ts:72-98; lib\story\fragments.ts (118 fragments, 10 titles, 2,786 words, counted via a bun probe run from the scratchpad); lib\futureMemory.ts:154-214; contexts\StoryContext.tsx:158-205 (proof appended after the composed paragraphs), :222-223 and :247 (old story filtered out), :231-253 (chapter++ on every regenerate); app\story\[id].tsx:105-116 (refresh calls regenerate); grep shows `mood` used only in UserContext/onboarding. Probe output: 'consecutive-chapter identical bridge actions: 52 of 300'.
findings.implication_for_vela:
The best way to say 'much more' while staying distinctive under 4.3 is to deepen the engine, not to add generic features:
- keep a chapter archive (a Memory Book)
- add a dedicated proof beat after arrival with did/moved/learned templates, using all prior proofs
- use mood
- give bridge actions an avoid-set, a bigger pool, and follow-ups that depend on the kind of proof
- make 'Weave chapter' depend on proof, separate from 'rewrite this chapter'
All of this is pure TypeScript that bun can test.

findings.title: Data-layer hazard: stale snapshot in the contexts silently drops writes
findings.detail: Every mutation in Story, Journal, Ritual and Board contexts is a useCallback over the current `data` snapshot, building `next` from it (e.g. `actions: [action, ...data.actions]`). A handler that calls two mutations on the same context in sequence keeps the old function references. For example, `await saveEvidence(...); await regenerate(id)` (the obvious 'record proof and weave' flow for v2): regenerate reads `data.actions` from before the proof and writes it back, deleting the completed proof. This doesn't happen today only because each screen does one write per context. Persistence also rewrites the whole blob with no write queue, and storage keys have no migration framework beyond the ad-hoc v1 parse. The chapter archive in the previous finding needs a schema change too (`vela.stories.v1` to v2 with a migration that keeps the current story as chapter N; earlier chapters are already gone for existing users).
findings.evidence: contexts\StoryContext.tsx:149-156 (persist), :231-253 (regenerate closes over data), :255-278 (saveEvidence), deps arrays [data, persist, render]; contexts\JournalContext.tsx:222-266; contexts\BoardContext.tsx:379-415; contexts\RitualContext.tsx:85-98. Found by reading the code, not by running it.
findings.implication_for_vela: One agent should refactor the contexts to reducer/functional updates with a serialized persist queue and add a v2 schema with chapters[], before any screen agent builds compound flows. Otherwise the v2 features most likely to be built will lose user proof, which is the core asset of the loop.

findings.title: No shared component layer; styling drift makes any redesign a per-file rewrite
findings.detail: There is no components/ directory. 15 of the 18 route files each define their own StyleSheet. The same blocks repeat: `cta`/`ctaText` x10, `dock` x8, `close` x6, `ctaDisabled`/`ctaTextDisabled` x5, `card` x5, `header` x10, plus a hand-rolled 'halo' icon circle and the 7-dot constellation twice (Today and Evidence). theme.ts is good (colors/space/radius/type/cardShadow/accentGlow; only 3 stray rgba literals in screens). But it declares 'Four sizes, two weights' while screens use 13 other fontSize values (11, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 44), all serif ones untokenized. There is no background treatment: every screen is flat `colors.bg`, and the 'starfield shimmer' peak moment promised in PLAN.md was never built. Versions from node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json (expo 57.0.9).

- Native risk: very low. Formline (SDK 57.0.16) already shipped with 57.0.1 in its lock.

findings.title: Ambient soundscapes: expo-audio plus original procedural audio works today (tested)
findings.detail:
expo-audio ~57.0.3 (bundled), peer expo-asset (installed 57.0.8), package 1.3 MB unpacked, small JS.
- Web: yes (HTMLAudioElement; autoplay needs a user gesture, and Listen is a gesture).
- Native risk: low to moderate (new native module).
- Looping: `useAudioPlayer(require(...))` + `player.loop = true`.
- Lock-screen and evening 'drift off' playback need UIBackgroundModes=audio, set via app.json infoPlist or the expo-audio plugin option. App Review accepts it because real audio plays.
- Silent switch: Vela currently never sets an audio session. AVSpeechSynthesizer uses the app session (usesApplicationAudioSession defaults to true) in the default category, which respects the mute switch, so narration is probably silent on muted phones. `setAudioModeAsync({ playsInSilentMode: true, interruptionMode: mix/duck })` at startup should fix narration and soundscapes together. Plausible but not device-verified.

Original audio pipeline, verified in the scratchpad: Python 3.12.10 + numpy 1.26.4 + scipy 1.17.1 (no soundfile needed; scipy.io.wavfile) and ffmpeg 8.1.2 full build on PATH (native `aac`, `alac`, `libopus`, `libmp3lame` encoders). I generated a 60 s stereo drone: sine partials snapped to whole cycles over the loop length, plus pink noise shaped by FFT so it wraps circularly. That makes a sample-exact loop. Encoded with `ffmpeg -c:a aac -b:a 96k -movflags +faststart`, it came out at 733,178 bytes for 60.0 s (97.8 kbps), about 0.73 MB per minute. Four 2-minute soundscapes would be about 6 MB.

Risk: AAC encoder priming and padding can cause a small gap at the loop point in AVPlayer. Test on a device; fallbacks are crossfading two players or shipping CAF/ALAC for short loops.

This makes listening feel premium and justifies Plus (one scape free, all with Plus) without servers or licensed audio. Keep soundscapes inside the chapter player, not as a standalone sleep-sounds tab, which would drift toward the 4.3-risky generic category.

findings.title: expo-speech can do voice choice, rate control and word highlighting; the reader uses none of it
findings.detail:
expo-speech 57.0.1 is installed. SpeechOptions: language, pitch, rate, voice (identifier), volume, useApplicationAudioSession, onStart/onDone/onStopped/onError/onBoundary/onPause/onResume.
- iOS onBoundary comes from AVSpeechSynthesizerDelegate willSpeakRangeOfSpeechString, giving {charIndex, charLength}. That is enough for word-level highlighting.
- Web maps to SpeechSynthesisUtterance.onboundary (event object differs; headless Chrome has no voices, which doesn't affect screenshots).
- `getAvailableVoicesAsync` returns identifier/name/language/quality. iOS Swift only maps `.enhanced` to 'Enhanced', so Premium voices show up as 'Default'.

The reader currently sends the whole story as one utterance at fixed rate 0.88 and pitch 0.98: no paragraph highlight, no pauses between paragraphs, no voice or speed choice, no auto-scroll.

A per-paragraph queue (speak paragraph i, onDone moves to i+1 after a short silence) enables paragraph and word highlighting, auto-scroll, resume-from-paragraph and a progress bar. Users must download Enhanced voices in iOS Settings, so the app should prefer Enhanced English voices and show a hint.

It also keeps 'unlimited listens' as the core advantage over Stella. Put the pure queue and segmenting logic in lib/audio/narration.ts with bun tests.

Pattern found locally (not only in WSL): C:\Users\Gain John\Downloads\solve_problem\rork-scripture-mate\expo has:

- the `@bacons/apple-targets` ^5.0.0 plugin

findings.title: Share cards: react-native-view-shot plus expo-sharing are feasible, with two gotchas
findings.detail:
react-native-view-shot 5.1.0 (bundled; peer RN >=0.76; depends on html2canvas for web) and expo-sharing ~57.0.8.
- Native: low risk; captureRef of an off-screen card View, then shareAsync(fileUri, {mimeType: 'image/png'}).
- Web: view-shot goes through html2canvas (no backdrop-filter, partial gradient fidelity), and expo-sharing needs navigator.share with files (missing in desktop Chrome). Use isAvailableAsync() and fall back to download or copy.
- Gotcha 1: once an image reaches the iOS share sheet, 'Save Image' requires NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription. Vela only declares NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, so add the Add key or that action can crash (well-known TCC rule, not device-verified here).
- Gotcha 2: the existing affirmation share is text-only via RN Share.

Card ideas that stay inside the loop: a chapter line card, a 'proof constellation' card showing N points of proof with the user's own sentence (private by default, opt-in), and a 7-day arc card. Drawing cards with react-native-svg plus gradients keeps the web capture faithful. Sharing is a zero-cost growth channel, and per memory the ASO baseline for Vela was 28 impressions and 1 download in 30 days.

findings.title: Not worth it for v2: Skia, Lottie, expo-image (low priority)

@shopify/react-native-skia 2.6.2 (bundled):

findings.title: Release pipeline, version state and the native version-skew trap
findings.detail:
Version state: app.json version 1.0.1, ios.buildNumber '4'; package.json 1.0.1; eas.json `appVersionSource: local`, production `autoIncrement: false`. The next release must raise these by hand, for example to 1.1.0 and build 5.

Build path: .github/workflows/ios-release.yml runs on macos-26 (Xcode 26 asserted) on every push to `review-rebuild` and on workflow_dispatch with a `submit` input. Steps: npm ci --include=dev, bun 1.3.14 test, tsc, check_metadata.py, `eas build --local --non-interactive --profile production`, upload the IPA artifact, optional altool upload with ASC_* secrets.
- The repo Dhaxor/vela is public, so runners are free and the EAS cloud quota isn't used.
- eas.json submit points at `../rork-scripture-mate/expo/credentials/AuthKey.p8` (local only).
- ios-e2e.yml (macos-14, Appium) runs on push to `e2e-run` and needs a simulator build URL pasted into APP_URL (devicetest profile, EAS cloud).

Branches: review-rebuild = 15c43a7 (shipping); `elevate-1.1` was created today at the same commit; main is stale at 75af97c. Baseline iOS Hermes bundle: 5.85 MB (Aug 29 export). 1.0.1 build 4 was submitted 2026-09-24 per memory; current ASC status not checked here.

Skew trap: expo-store-review is pinned exactly to 57.0.1 because 57.0.2+ needs SceneGeometry from a newer expo-modules-core, and the archive failed against 57.0.8. Vela is on expo 57.0.9 / expo-modules-core 57.0.8, while npm latest is 57.0.30 and Formline builds on 57.0.16 / emc 57.0.13. New expo-* modules added with `~` ranges can resolve to patches that compile only on macOS archive. tsc, bun and web will not catch this.

findings.title: Concrete bugs and gaps to fix during the redesign
findings.detail:
(1) The Evidence success card over-counts: `lit = index < min(7, points.length + 1)`, but `points` already contains the just-saved proof after re-render, so the first proof lights 2 stars (visible in the audit capture).
(2) Today shows '1 moments have shaped your arc' (no pluralization).
(3) proofConstellation buckets by UTC (`toISOString().slice(0,10)`) while streaks use local dates. The caption says 'Seven days', but it shows the last 7 distinct days that had a proof, not a 7-day window.
(4) The Evidence back button uses raw `router.back()`, not `safeBack`. That is the GO_BACK crash class fixed in 68bd16a, and it will trigger once widgets or notifications deep-link straight to /evidence.
(5) Today and its weave button only consider `intents[0]`, so Plus users with several arcs can't reach the others from Today.
(6) Paywall benefit 'All journal templates, forever' isn't backed by any gate; the journal is fully free, and the listing description repeats the claim.
(7) Onboarding's ritual choice never schedules reminders. Reminders exist only as Settings buttons with Alert feedback (a no-op on web). Times are fixed at 08:00/21:00 with static copy, there's no setNotificationHandler or response listener, and Settings can't edit name, ritual time or reminder time.
(8) Journal 'Past pages' aren't tappable, and board photos are saved with an empty caption and no caption UI.
(9) The reader's Listen dock overlaps body text with no scrim.
