findings.title: Testing and verification surface
findings.detail: bun test covers only the pure modules (engine determinism, slot filling with awkward input, avoid-set exhaustion, futureMemory, streak, journal 369 caps, notifications specs, purchase classification and gating, review-prompt gate). There are no context or component tests; React Native modules are kept out of bun via lazy `require` seams (notifications, reviewPrompt, PlusContext, BoardContext). The web build (`vela-web` launch config, port 8094, metro) is the visual QA and screenshot surface: every interactive element has a testID, which becomes data-testid on web and drives store/shots/audit.mjs. The Appium e2e on simulator is stale (previous finding). tsc is strict with typed routes, though Evidence routes need `as never` casts.

Each screen agent should check its work through the web harness at SCALE=3, and the release gate should include one native CI build.

recommendations: STEP 0, one agent, serial, blocking. Owns package.json, package-lock.json and app.json only. (a) Add exact pins (no ~): expo-linear-gradient 57.0.1, expo-font 57.0.1 (made direct), one or two @expo-google-fonts families (e.g. fraunces or newsreader 0.4.1 for serif display/story, inter 0.4.2 for UI so web screenshots match iOS), expo-audio 57.0.3, react-native-view-shot 5.1.0, expo-sharing 57.0.8; optionally expo-blur 57.0.2. Consider moving expo to Formline's proven 57.0.16 in the same commit. (b) app.json: NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription, UIBackgroundModes audio, and later ios.appleTeamId 6RMFGXBQ82 plus the App Group for widgets. (c) Run npm ci, bun test, tsc, web start, then ONE workflow_dispatch release build (submit=false) on elevate-1.1 to catch native compile skew (the expo-store-review SceneGeometry trap) before any screen work.

STEP 1a, one agent (design-system owner). Extend constants/theme.ts without renaming existing tokens, so untouched screens still compile:
- `fonts` (display, serif, sans families)
- a `serifType` scale that replaces the 13 ad-hoc sizes
- `gradients` (night, aurora, gold sheen stop arrays)
- `motion` (durations/easing; twinkle/drift periods)
- `glow` levels and z-layers
Then build components/ui/ with a barrel index.ts:
- Screen: safe area + NightSky background + scroll/keyboard handling + header and dock slots + `still` flag
- NightSky: seeded Starfield (mulberry32 from lib/story/rng) of SVG/Animated dots with Reanimated 4 CSS-keyframe twinkle, plus Aurora as LinearGradient/SVG RadialGradient layers; variants calm/reveal/dawn
- GlowCard: pressable, scale feedback, tinted border, optional gold/aurora glow and sheen
- PrimaryButton / SecondaryButton / GhostButton: 52-56pt, disabled state, haptics
- IconButton: 44pt, required accessibilityLabel
- Header: back/close/title/right, using safeBack
- Dock: bottom CTA with gradient scrim
- SectionHeader and Eyebrow
- Chip / ChipGroup
- TextField: serif or sans variant
- Text: T variant='display|title|body|caption|serifDisplay|serifBody'
- Halo: glowing icon disc
- ProgressDots
- ConfirmSheet: replaces Alert.alert and works on web
- Toast
Add a __DEV__-only /dev/kitchen-sink route for visual QA. Freeze the API after review.

STEP 1b, in parallel, data/engine agent. Owns contexts/StoryContext.tsx, lib/story/*, lib/futureMemory.ts and their tests.
- Reducer/functional updates plus a serialized persist queue (fixes the stale-snapshot write loss).
- Schema `vela.stories.v2` with a per-intent chapters[] archive, migrated from v1 by keeping the current story as chapter N.
- Selectors: chaptersForIntent, proofsForIntent, activeIntentId (user-selectable, replacing intents[0]).
- Engine v2: a dedicated 'proof' beat after arrival with did/moved/learned templates that can reference the last 1-3 proofs; mood-aware opening/closing; at least double the arrival/living/title pools with original writing.
- Bridge actions: 8-10 per focus with an avoid-set, plus follow-ups keyed to the last proof kind.
- Split 'Weave next chapter' (requires a new proof) from 'Re-render this chapter' (no chapter++).
- Fix UTC vs local dateKey and the constellation window semantics. All covered by bun tests.

STEP 1c, in parallel, audio agent. Owns scripts/gen_soundscapes.py, assets/audio/, lib/audio/* and tests.
- Generate 4 original 90-120 s loops with numpy/scipy: whole-cycle partials plus FFT-circular noise; night, rain-on-glass, dawn birds-free shimmer, hearth crackle via filtered impulses.
- Encode with ffmpeg `-c:a aac -b:a 96k -movflags +faststart` (about 0.73 MB/min measured).
- lib/audio/narration.ts: pure paragraph segmentation and queue state, with onBoundary {charIndex, charLength} mapped to paragraph/word indices.
- useNarration/useSoundscape hooks: expo-speech per-paragraph queue, Enhanced-voice preference, rate options; expo-audio looping bed with ducking.
- Call `setAudioModeAsync({ playsInSilentMode: true })` at startup; verify on a device that narration is no longer silent on muted phones and that the loop has no AAC gap.

STEP 1d, in parallel, optional, widget agent. Owns targets/vela-widget/ and lib/widgets/.
- Copy the Scripture Mate pattern (rork-scripture-mate/expo/targets/verse-widget, lib/widgetBridge.ts, services/studyWidgets.ts): versioned JSON snapshot {chapterTitle, bridgeText, constellation[7], streak, intentId} written via ExtensionStorage('group.app.vela.manifest') behind requireOptionalNativeModule, then reloadWidget.
- SwiftUI systemSmall/Medium plus accessoryRectangular, with widgetURL vela://evidence/<intentId>.
- The 15.1 podspec patch is probably unnecessary on SDK 57 (Expo floor 16.4); confirm after prebuild.
- Plan for one interactive EAS signing run by the owner for the new extension bundle id. Ship v2 without widgets if this blocks.

STEP 2, parallel screen agents. Start only after the Step 1a primitives and Step 1b data API are frozen. Each agent owns disjoint files and imports components/ui only:
- A: app/onboarding.tsx (NightSky reveal, back navigation, mood used downstream, schedule reminders on the ritual step)
- B: app/(tabs)/index.tsx + components/feature/{ProofConstellation (SVG stars joined by lines, tap for the proof sentence), BridgeCard, ArcSwitcher}
- C: app/story/[id].tsx + app/story/new.tsx + components/feature/{NarrationPlayer, SoundscapePicker} (karaoke highlight, scrimmed dock, starfield reveal peak)
- D: app/evidence/[intentId].tsx + components/feature/ShareCard + lib/share/ (safeBack, fix the double-lit star, a celebratory peak)
- E: app/(tabs)/stories.tsx + new app/arc/[intentId].tsx (Memory Book: chapter timeline with woven proofs)
- F: app/(tabs)/journal.tsx + app/journal/* (prompts seeded from the active desire; past-page detail)
- G: app/(tabs)/board.tsx + app/affirmation.tsx + app/affirmations.tsx (captions, link cards to an arc, ConfirmSheet)
- H: app/paywall.tsx + app/settings.tsx (real Plus value, e.g. multiple arcs, all soundscapes, Memory Book export/share themes; drop the unbacked 'journal templates' claim; name/ritual/reminder-time editing)
- I: app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx (blurred or Liquid Glass tab bar).
Keep every existing testID and add one for each new control.

Keep the 4.3-safe framing in every addition. Each new feature should visibly feed, show or replay the Future Memory loop: chapter archive, proof beat, bridge reminders and widget, proof share cards, narrated chapter with a soundscape bed. Avoid standalone generic surfaces (a sleep-sounds tab, a quote feed, a horoscope-style daily card) that would make Vela look like other manifestation apps again. Update store/REVIEW_RESPONSE_4_3.md and the review path to match.

STEP 3, screenshots and release.
- Commit store/shots/{audit.mjs, cdp.mjs} under scripts/shots/.
- Add a web `still` mode (URL flag or EXPO_PUBLIC_SHOTS): freeze NightSky, no blur, fixed clock/greeting, seed localStorage with a curated multi-chapter arc and proofs, real configured prices on the paywall only in this mode.
- Capture with W=430 H=932 SCALE=3 to get native 1290x2796.
- Make @resvg/resvg-js a devDependency (drop the ../../formline import) and render 6-8 frames using the bundled display font, plus composited widget and share-card frames.
- Fix e2e/walkthrough.mjs (`~ritual-story` to `~future-memory-card`, add the evidence-to-weave steps).
- Bump app.json to 1.1.0 / buildNumber '5' (manual: appVersionSource local, autoIncrement false), merge elevate-1.1 into review-rebuild to trigger the macos-26 build, then dispatch with submit=true.

research.summary:
I viewed all 30 audit captures, the 5 contact sheets, the 3 live App Store screenshots and the app icon, and read every file in app/ plus constants/theme.ts. In this report, [audit] means C:\Users\GAINJO~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Gain-John-Downloads-solve-problem\f6853cbe-5ed2-4f58-8cba-218452638bb6\scratchpad\vela-audit.

Vela looks limited mainly because it has no visual layer at all. Every screen is a flat #0B0A18 background with the same rounded indigo cards. react-native-svg is a dependency but no file imports it. The app has no gradients, images or custom fonts. The serif is whatever the platform supplies: Times New Roman on the web build that the store shots are taken from, Georgia on iOS. The best brand asset, the sail-and-star app icon (Vela is the constellation of the Sails), never appears inside the app. The welcome screen uses lucide's generic Sparkles glyph instead.

The feature that sets Vela apart, the proof constellation, is drawn as a row of 7 dots with a "1 moments" grammar bug. The peak moment (saving a proof) is a stock check-circle card. At the story's end the upsell outranks the loop's own next step: "See Plus" is a filled gold button while "Make it observable" is a text link.

The 60/30/10 color rule is broken in practice. Gold appears in about 7 places on one Today viewport, and every selected state turns a muddy brown. The theme promises 4 font sizes but the app uses 15. The live App Store screenshots are blurry, crop the UI mid-word, show an unlabeled gold bar, and repeat the "1 moments" bug.

The proposed Visual System v2 rebrands Vela as a "star atlas / celestial navigation" product. It has five parts:
- a procedural night sky seeded from the user's data
- faint star-chart line work
- a loop color code: gold = the future chapter, violet = the bridge, warm starlight = proof
- the type pairing Newsreader + Instrument Sans (both OFL)
- a set of named signature moments (First Light, Charting, The Weave, Star Birth, Named Sky)

All of it is built from SVG and Reanimated and renders on react-native-web. It is also distinct from Stella, whose look is a light pink/lavender gradient with an iridescent orb. That matters for Guideline 4.3. This was a research-only pass and I modified no repo files.

findings.title: No atmosphere or imagery: every screen is a flat near-black background with the same rounded indigo cards
findings.detail:
All 30 screens share one recipe: background #0B0A18, cards #1C1A3A with a 1px hairline border, radius 24/28, a lucide icon in a tinted circle, a gold pill CTA. There is no gradient, texture, illustration, photo, depth layering or ambient motion anywhere. react-native-svg 15.15.4 is in package.json but a grep for 'react-native-svg|Svg|LinearGradient|BlurView|useFonts|Canvas' across app/, lib/ and contexts/ returns nothing. There is no components/ folder, so every screen hand-rolls its own cards.

The welcome hero (01) is a lucide Sparkles icon in a brown circle. In 2025–26 that glyph is the universal 'AI feature' symbol, so it reads as generic rather than mystical. The brand's best asset, assets/icon.png (a gold sail with a 4-point star, i.e. Vela, 'the Sails'), never appears inside the app. Compared with category leaders:
- Calm sells atmosphere: full-bleed living scenes.
- Headspace has its own illustration system.
- Finch makes growth visible: a pet that grows.
- Stoic has editorial typography and insight charts.

Vela currently has none of these, so it reads as a well-spaced form, not a place.

research.summary: Vela's Future Memory loop (chapter → bridge → proof → next chapter) is a strong, distinctive idea, but the build is thin in exactly the places that make it distinctive. That is the main reason it feels "limited". The arc keeps no memory of itself: each new chapter overwrites the last, so past chapters can't be re-read and past proofs have no screen of their own. The "proof woven into the next chapter" mechanic is one fixed sentence with a visible double-period glitch. It only ever uses the latest proof, re-weaves it into later chapters, and the unlabeled refresh icon in the reader moves the chapter number forward with no proof at all. Nothing brings a user back tomorrow. Onboarding asks "When do we meet?" but never schedules a reminder (reminders exist only behind a Settings row, at fixed 8:00/21:00 with generic copy). Chapter 2 can also be opened right away, which contradicts the success screen's "Tomorrow's chapter will remember it". The main reading moment is plain serif text fading in on a flat background, read by the system voice. The Listen pill sits over the text, and the bridge card and a Plus upsell appear before the story has finished revealing. The app is named after a constellation and promises a "proof constellation", yet it has no sky: react-native-svg is installed but no screen uses it, and the constellation is 7 grey dots. The counts are also wrong: "1 moments", 2 stars lit on the success card against 1 on Today, and a "Seven days" caption that isn't about days. Supporting features don't connect to the loop: the Board is empty with blank photo captions, journal entries can't be opened, affirmations are a generic library, and the Stories tab is a whole tab for one card. A paying user hits a regression: Today only shows intents[0], so adding a second dream hides the first arc and its proofs. The submitted App Store screenshots are clipped mid-sentence and show the "1 moments" bug. Solution: open with the user's own arc stats; benefits that deepen the loop (concurrent arcs, soundscapes and sleep timer, a 'Book of Proof' PDF keepsake via expo-print on the device, cover-art themes, all affirmation areas) while the free single-arc loop stays complete; move the soft nudge to after the first proof or chapter 2; contextual entry points (second dream, soundscape tap, export tap, after a milestone celebration); per-month equivalent on yearly; any trial clearly labelled; no countdowns. Screens: paywall, reader nudge, Arc, Sky. Expected impact: higher conversion with honest framing that fits the 'generous free tier' brand.

13. Reshoot the App Store screenshots once items 1-5 land. Problem: the current 4.3-rebuild set is clipped mid-sentence, has an unlabeled CTA and shows the '1 moments' bug, and none shows the emotional payoff. Solution: a set of 6-8: the materializing chapter with the user's words in gold; proof → the same sentence woven into chapter 2 (side by side); the living constellation; the Arc timeline; the overnight-ready lock-screen notification; Wall/journal; and the private/offline/unlimited-listens promise. Fix the capture viewport. Screens: store assets. Expected impact: product-page conversion, and the screenshots double as the story for any future 4.3 review.

research.summary: I read the whole content layer (engine, fragments, rng, futureMemory, affirmations, journal, focus, their tests, StoryContext and the screens that render them) and ran throwaway bun scripts from the scratchpad (content_probe/*.ts) to generate and measure stories. The writing in each fragment is good, but the system around it is thin and has visible defects. In total there are 118 story fragments (about 2,800 words), 10 titles shared by every focus, 18 bridge actions (3 per focus), 1 evidence template, 120 affirmations, 12 scripting prompts, 9 gratitude stems and 2 notification texts. A story is about 160 words, roughly a minute of TTS. The desire slot breaks in two ways. First, 9 of the 36 arrival frames break the sentence for verb-shaped desires like "to open my bakery", which the engine's own tests and header comment list as a supported shape. Second, every frame leaves first-person "my/I" inside second-person narration. The repo's own audit screenshot shows this live: "you built it, brick by honest brick, into my own design studio, with clients who trust my eye." Personalization is shallow. The desire appears once per story, the name appears in only 29–42% of stories, the chosen feeling in 22%, and about half of stories contain neither. Onboarding collects mood and ritual time, but mood is never read and ritual time only sets reminder hours. A "chapter" is just a reroll: tapping refresh moves the counter up, every chapter uses the same wake-to-sleep day with the desire already fully achieved, and earlier chapters are deleted. Evidence is not woven into the story. It is appended after the "sleep now" closing with doubled punctuation ("agencies.. It is"). The same proof repeats in every later chapter until a new one is logged, and the proof type (did/moved/learned) is ignored. Repetition is guaranteed from chapter 7, and from chapter 12 on about 0.9 of 7 paragraphs on average match the previous chapter. The previous chapter's bridge action repeats 20% of the time. The supporting rituals repeat quickly too, and the Plus benefit "All journal templates" refers to nothing that is gated. The fix is a person-aware desire shaper (prototyped: about 60 lines handles 12 of 15 realistic desires), plus a staged 7-chapter season, desire-motif lexicons, daypart variants, real proof weaving, letters from your future self and guided eyes-closed sessions. That is roughly 30–45k words of original text, all on-device. It deepens the Future Memory loop rather than drifting toward a generic affirmation app.

findings.title: Desire splicing breaks grammar and voice (live in the shipped UI)
findings.detail: normalizeDesire only trims and lowercases. It does not change person or sentence shape. 9 of the 36 arrival frames put {desire} where only a noun phrase fits, which breaks the file's own stated rule (fragments.ts lines 8-10 say {desire} goes only after a colon, a dash, or 'that…is'). Rendered with the engine's own example input 'to open my bakery', you get: 'built it, brick by honest brick, into to open my bakery' (ar-ca3), 'It adds up to to open my bakery' (ar-pe2), 'This is to open my bakery, in practice' (ar-pe1), 'the life where to open my bakery is just how things are' (ar-love6), 'about to open my bakery' (ar-co4), plus ar-ca6, ar-co2, ar-co6 and ar-he2. Imperative goals, which are common, go wrong in every frame: 'Find my soulmate' becomes 'It's true now: find my soulmate.' 'I want…' desires contradict the already-true premise: 'That's the miracle nobody claps for: I want to be debt free by next summer, settled into routine.' Any 'my/I' desire leaves first person inside second-person narration (all 36 of 36 frames). The app also teaches users to write 'I am…' lines: the 369 placeholder is 'e.g. I am paid well for work I love' and the vision board says 'Write the goal as already true…'. Only the intake placeholder suggests a noun phrase. The e2e walkthrough only ever types the safe noun phrase 'a home that feels like rest'.

findings.implication_for_vela: The first line of the product's emotional peak, where the user's own words come back, is the line most likely to read as broken. App reviewers and users judge a template engine by exactly this. A shape- and person-aware shaper fixes it on-device: the prototype in content_probe/shaper.ts is about 60 lines with a 33-verb table and correctly handles 12 of 15 realistic desires ('Find my soulmate' becomes 'you found your soulmate' or 'finding your soulmate'; 'I want to be debt free by next summer' becomes 'you are debt free').

findings.title: Chapters are rerolls, not an arc, and the arc's history is deleted
findings.detail: regenerate() runs on both the reader's refresh icon and Today's 'Weave chapter N', and adds 1 to the chapter every time, with or without proof. Ten taps on refresh give 'chapter 11'. Every chapter is the same 7-beat day: wake, already-achieved arrival, sensory, midday, someone notices, gratitude, sleep. Chapter 1 already shows the desire fully achieved ('it happened. It's real now'), so later chapters have nothing left to move toward. Titles come from one global pool of 10, carry no chapter number or stage, and never use the user's words. Each new chapter replaces the last ('One living story per intent'), so the Stories tab holds one card per intent and earlier chapters can't be reread. The proof constellation only shows the last 7 distinct days.
findings.evidence: contexts/StoryContext.tsx:230-250 (chapter = intent.chapter + 1 on every regenerate; stories filter at :247 drops previous chapters); app/story/[id].tsx again() on the RefreshCw icon; lib/story/engine.ts BEAT_ORDER; lib/story/fragments.ts TITLES (10, focus-agnostic); lib/futureMemory.ts proofConstellation .slice(-7); vela-sheet-4.jpg 20-stories.png (one card)
findings.implication_for_vela: 'Future Memory' is what got Vela past Guideline 4.3, but the narrative layer under it is a slot machine with a counter. Users should be able to feel the story progress and look back over a growing book of their future. That needs staged chapters, proof-gated progression, a reroll that doesn't advance the chapter, and a kept archive.

findings.title: Evidence is appended, not woven, and the bridge is defective
findings.detail: evidenceBridge is one fixed template added as the last paragraph, after the closing (which is usually about falling asleep). It doesn't use sanitizeEvidence's trailing punctuation, so typical input produces 'I sent the proposal.. It is small…' and 'Booked my first client call!. It is…'. It quotes first-person text into second-person narration. The proof type is captured but never used. regenerate() takes the most recent action with evidence, so the same proof paragraph comes back word for word in every later chapter until a new proof is logged. Only the latest proof is ever used, so no chapter recalls the earlier ones. Related proof-surface copy bugs: the evidence success screen lights 2 stars for a first proof (lit = index < points.length + 1, where points already includes the new proof; visible as two gold dots in 16-evidence-success), and Today shows '1 moments have shaped your arc.'
findings.evidence: lib/futureMemory.ts:76-84 (sanitizeEvidence keeps final punctuation; template at :83); contexts/StoryContext.tsx:172-178 (proof appended after closing), :236-238 (latestEvidence reused); app/evidence/[intentId].tsx:126; app/(tabs)/index.tsx:129; vela-sheet-3.jpg (16-evidence-success, 17/19-today); repro output: content_probe/tics.ts and samples.ts (Maya ch2 and ch3 both end with the same 'agencies..' paragraph)
findings.implication_for_vela: 'Proof is woven into the next chapter' is the main claim of the 4.3 rebuild and of the store screenshots. Right now it is a postscript with a typo and it goes stale. Proper weaving would be kind-specific lines placed inside the narrative, used once per proof, with older proofs recalled by date. That is the cheapest change that makes the loop feel alive, and it shows up directly in screenshots.

findings.title: Small pools mean guaranteed repeats from chapter 7, then random repeats
findings.detail: Per focus, a user draws from opening 10, arrival 6, sensory 10, living 6, witness 8, gratitude 8, closing 10, titles 10. That is 58 pieces, even though the theoretical count is 23M combinations per focus. The avoid-set grows forever. Once a pool is used up (arrival and living after 6 chapters), pickAvoiding falls back to the full pool with no memory of recent picks. Simulated over 2,000 users and 30 chapters with the real app logic: all 2,000 hit their first repeated paragraph at exactly chapter 7. The average number of paragraphs identical to the previous chapter goes 0.34 at ch7, 0.59 at ch10, 0.90 at ch12, 0.92 at ch20. Fixed phrases repeat across stories: 'now' appears 2.05 times per story (35 of 118 fragments), and 'Tuesday' is hard-coded in 3 fragments and 1 title.
findings.evidence: lib/story/rng.ts:31 (fallback to the full pool); contexts/StoryContext.tsx:170 (avoid = all usedIds ever); scratchpad content_probe/gen.ts (pool sizes) and stats.ts (simulation output: first repeat at ch7 = 2000/2000)
findings.implication_for_vela: Stella's known weak spot is repetitive content, and Vela's pitch is 'no two renderings repeat'. A daily user sees that promise fail after about a week. Two fixes: a recency-window avoid (don't reuse anything from the last N chapters, where N is about half the pool) instead of a permanent set, and pools 3–5x larger with stage tags.

findings.title: Personalization is thin, and data that is already collected goes unused
findings.detail: In 10,000 seeded stories per focus, {name} appears in 29.4% of stories (love, career) to 41.6% (health). The chosen feeling appears in only 21.7% (2 of 118 fragments use it). Between 45% and 55% of stories contain neither. {desire} appears exactly once per story, in the arrival beat. Nothing else in the story follows from what the user wanted. Arrival and living fragments are generic to the focus and can contradict the desire: debt-free gets 'money moving toward you while you sleep… became a system'; a half marathon gets 'appetite, sleep, breath in rhythm' with no race anywhere; 5 of the 12 love fragments assume a romantic partner you live with (bed, keys in the bowl, hand on the small of your back), even for 'heal my relationship with my mum'. Onboarding asks for mood (hopeful/stuck/tired/certain) and ritual time (morning/evening/both). Mood is stored and never read. Ritual time only sets reminder hours.
findings.evidence: scratchpad content_probe/stats.ts (presence table); content_probe/samples.ts (Sam/abundance, Priya/health outputs); lib/story/fragments.ts love arrival/living fragments; app/onboarding.tsx:59-64 MOODS; contexts/UserContext.tsx:24,52 (mood stored, no reader; grep finds no profile.mood use); lib/notifications.ts (the only ritual consumer)
findings.implication_for_vela: The advantage of on-device generation is supposed to be 'it's about me'. Right now a story is about 160 words of generic text with one spliced phrase. Matching desire keywords to motif packs, using mood and daypart, and using the name and feeling in more beats would make each story read as written for this user, with no server and no LLM.

findings.title: Bridge actions: 18 total, generic, and often repeated
findings.detail: deriveFutureAction hashes (focus, desire, chapter) mod 3. The desire text only affects which of 3 fixed lines is picked. 19.8% of chapters get the same action as the previous chapter (Maya ch1 = ch2, Priya ch1 = ch2, Sam ch1 = ch3 in the samples). Actions never mention the desire. Sam ('debt free') got 'Take one five-minute step toward an opportunity you have been circling.' There is no ladder of difficulty, no link to the arc stage, and no follow-up based on the last proof type.
findings.evidence: lib/futureMemory.ts:24-75 (ACTIONS 3 per focus; :72 index = hash % 3); scratchpad content_probe/stats.ts ('bridge action identical to previous chapter's: 19.8%') and samples.ts
findings.implication_for_vela: The bridge is the part of the loop that turns imagination into an observable action. It is the most distinctive, most screenshot-worthy part of Vela and the most clearly not spam. It needs a real library (tiered, staged, matched to motifs, never repeated back-to-back) more than any other content.

findings.title: Time of day doesn't follow the user's ritual, and time runs backwards in some stories
findings.detail: All 10 openings are waking up and all 10 closings are falling asleep, so a morning-ritual user listening at 8am hears 'Sleep now'. The shared sensory pool includes se9 'Evening light comes early…', which lands between the morning arrival and the midday living beat about 10% of the time, so the day goes morning, evening, midday. The 8:00 reminder promises 'Three quiet minutes', but a story is about 160 words, roughly a minute of TTS at rate 0.88. The domain-word splice gives odd lines: se8 'Hunger without anxiety turns out to be one of work's / self-belief's / calm's quietest gifts'.
findings.evidence: lib/story/fragments.ts opening op1-op10, closing cl1-cl10, se8 (line 113), se9 (line 114); lib/notifications.ts morning body; app/story/[id].tsx Speech rate 0.88; content_probe/gen.ts (about 160 words per story)
findings.implication_for_vela: Morning and evening variants are a cheap fix that is easy to notice. Users who picked 'Morning: set the day before it sets you' should get a chapter that ends with them heading out into the day. They also allow a longer, slower session that actually delivers the 'three quiet minutes'.

findings.title: Supporting-ritual content repeats quickly, and Plus has little exclusive depth
findings.detail: Affirmations: 20 per focus, drawn daily with replacement. A single-area user sees about 14.3 repeats per 30 days and gets yesterday's line again 4.4% of the time. 26 of the 120 affirmations share a 4-word run with a story fragment ('Stairs are just stairs', 'No is a full sentence', 'without rehearsing the walk'), so users keep hearing the same phrases. Journal: 12 scripting prompts that ignore focus and intent, with a repeat in 46 of 52 weeks and yesterday's prompt again on 34 of 363 days. 9 gratitude stems, 3 per day, overlapping yesterday's on 298 of 363 days. 369 has no suggested phrases. The paywall lists 'All journal templates, forever', but none of the 3 journal practices is gated. 'Every affirmation pack' means 20 lines for each of the 5 other areas.
findings.evidence: lib/affirmations.ts (120 lines, dailyAffirmation); lib/journal.ts SCRIPT_PROMPTS (12), GRATITUDE_STEMS (9); app/paywall.tsx:29-34 BENEFITS; no isPlus in app/journal/* (grep); scratchpad content_probe/stats.ts (repeat and overlap numbers)
findings.implication_for_vela: These rituals are where daily habit forms, and they repeat within days. Content depth is also the honest way to give Plus value without capping listens: guided sessions, letters, extra seasons and deeper packs give Plus something real to unlock while the free core stays generous.

findings.title: Tests check slot filling, not language quality
findings.detail: engine.test.ts checks that no '{slot}' text is left, that dollar signs pass through, and that the avoid-set works up to pool size. No test renders realistic desire shapes into every frame or checks the evidence bridge's punctuation. The normalizeDesire test treats 'To open my bakery' as a supported case, yet that same input produces 'into to open my bakery'. Nothing checks repetition across a long chapter run.
findings.evidence: lib/story/engine.test.ts:15-27, 58-77; lib/futureMemory.test.ts:12-23
findings.implication_for_vela: Before the pools grow 5x, add a golden test matrix: about 30 realistic desires × every {desire} frame, plus regex checks for 'to to', 'into to|into I', '\.\.', '!\.' and 'my' inside narration. Add a 30-chapter repetition test that fails on any back-to-back repeat. Without these, a bigger content set will bring more of the same defects.

recommendations: P0 – Desire shaper (about 150 lines plus a 150-verb table, with tests): detect the desire's shape (noun phrase / 'to'-verb / bare or imperative verb / 'I…' clause / 'I want…'). Remove want-verbs and deadline tails ('by next summer', 'this year', 'before my wedding'). Swap my→your, I am→you are, me→you. Expose three slot forms: {desire.quote} (the user's exact words in quotation marks, always safe: 'the line you wrote — "…"'), {desire.np} ('finding your soulmate', 'your own design studio') and {desire.done} ('you found your soulmate', 'you are debt free'). Rewrite the 9 frames that break the rule. Change the intake microcopy to 'Say it however it comes out' so 369 and board users' 'I am…' habit stops causing problems. Prototype: scratchpad content_probe/shaper.ts.

P0 – Proof weaving v2: (a) trim the evidence's trailing .!? and render it as a quote or in second person; (b) write 3 kinds × 3 positions (inside arrival, as the 'witness', just before the closing) × 6 variants = about 54 original lines, e.g. did: 'You remember the afternoon you {evidence} — it's where this morning began.' learned: 'Reality taught you something: "{evidence}." Future-you kept it.'; (c) use each proof once (track proofUsedInChapter); (d) from chapter 4 on, recall older proofs by date ('Twelve days ago you wrote…'), about 12 recall lines; (e) fix the 2-star first-proof bug and '1 moments' pluralization.

P0 – Repetition and chapter semantics: replace the permanent avoid-set with a recency window (avoid ids from the last ⌊pool/2⌋ chapters plus never the immediately previous chapter). Split 'reroll this chapter' (refresh icon, no chapter++) from 'weave next chapter' (offered after a proof or 24h). Keep every chapter: the Stories tab becomes the book of this future, with chapter cards and their proofs. Show every proof in the constellation, not just the last 7 days. Add a 30-chapter no-back-to-back test.

P1 – Seasons (staged arcs): each intent runs a 7-chapter season, and each chapter is a different scene, not the same day again. 1 The First Glimpse (first morning inside it), 2 The Night Before (rehearsal), 3 The Hard Day (something goes wrong and future-you handles it; realistic and unlike competitors), 4 Someone Notices, 5 The Threshold (the first 60 seconds after the news), 6 The Ordinary Tuesday (integration), 7 The Letter Back (future self writes, quoting every proof). After the season, the user rewrites the desire for Season 2 using what they learned. Size: 7 scene skeletons with 5–7 beats each; focus-specific pools of about 8 per beat × 2 focus beats × 7 scenes × 6 focus ≈ 670 fragments, plus about 170 shared scene fragments. Titles: 60+ stage titles ('Chapter 3 · The Hard Day'). About 20–25k words.

P1 – Desire motif lexicon (the biggest single gain in vividness): about 40 archetypes matched on-device by keyword (studio/business, bakery/café, home/apartment, partner, wedding, family/baby, friendship, family repair, promotion, new job, freelancing, debt-free, savings/house deposit, travel, relocation, marathon/running, strength/gym, healing/recovery, sleep, public speaking, writing a book, music, art, exam/degree, visa or new country, etc.). Each archetype has 8 sensory details, 4 living moments, 3 witness lines and 5 bridge actions. That is about 800 short lines, about 12k words. Maya's story then contains fabric swatches, the studio door and a client email instead of generic sunlight.

P1 – Daypart and mood variants: read profile.ritual and the current hour. A morning chapter ends with the user heading into the day carrying the bridge action; an evening chapter ends in sleep; a midday 90-second reset is optional. Sizes: 3 dayparts × (12 openings + 12 closings) = 72, sensory split by daypart = 3 × 12 = 36, and 4 onboarding moods × 8 opening lines = 32 (a 'stuck' user gets 'the morning after the long stillness'). Remove se9 from the shared morning sequence.

P1 – Bridge action library: 3 → 25 per focus (150 total), each tagged with a tier (2-min / 10-min / brave 30-min), a season stage and optionally a motif ('Sketch the sign above your studio door'). Choose the next action based on the last proof type (learned → smaller retry, did → step up). Never repeat back-to-back. Add 3 preset 'reshape' alternatives per action.

P1 – Letters from your future self (fits the loop, and makes strong screenshots and shares): unlocked by the 1st, 3rd and 7th proof and by season end. Assembled from templates plus the user's proofs quoted with dates ('On 14 October you wrote "Sent my portfolio to two studios I admire." I still have that day.'). Size: 6 focus × 6 letters + 10 shared milestone letters ≈ 46 letters × about 200 words ≈ 9k words. Render as a shareable card that does not identify the user.

P1 (Plus) – Guided 'Step Inside' sessions, 5–10 min with eyes closed: settle (60 s of breath) → descend (a starfield countdown, fitting the Vela star theme) → enter this chapter's scene, slowed down and using motif lines → anchor (a thumb-to-finger 'proof anchor') → return with the bridge action spoken aloud. Built from expo-speech utterances chained with timed pauses. Size: 10 shared induction and return modules (about 150 words each), plus 6 focus × 3 scene scripts (about 900 words each) ≈ 18k words. Session length finally matches the reminder's 'three quiet minutes' promise and goes beyond it.

P2 (Plus) – Soundscape pairing with no licensing risk: generate on-device (brown/pink noise, a rain texture, a low 'night sky' drone tuned per focus) or bundle 6–8 self-recorded 2-minute AAC loops (about 1 MB each). Map them to focus × daypart (e.g. peace/evening = rain on glass, career/morning = soft café murmur). Mix under TTS with ducking. Needs an audio dependency such as expo-audio; there are no ongoing costs.

P2 – Ritual content depth: affirmations 120 → about 480 (60 core per focus with no shared phrasing with story fragments, plus 4 mood packs × 15, a 'hard day' pack of 30 and a 'sleep' pack of 30), plus proof-born lines derived from the user's own evidence ('I am someone who follows through'). Scripting prompts 12 → 120 (20 per focus), plus prompts tied to the current chapter ('Write the scene just after this chapter ends') and the open bridge, plus a Sunday Proof Review. Gratitude stems 9 → 60. Ten 369 phrase suggestions per focus, auto-generated through the shaper ('I {desire.done}'). Notification copy 2 → 50, including lines that echo the open bridge action. Draw daily picks without replacement so nothing repeats until the pool is exhausted.

P2 – Writing hygiene during the expansion: limit 'now' to 1 per story and phrase-family repeats to 1, retire the hard-coded 'Tuesday' (use the actual weekday, or none), split the love pools into romantic, family and friendship variants chosen by keywords, give the domain word per-focus phrasings (no 'work's quietest gifts'), and use {name} and {feeling} in at least 2 beats per story so every story contains both. Target totals: about 30–45k original words (currently about 2.8k), still well under 1 MB of text, all on-device. Every addition hangs off chapter → bridge → proof, so the 4.3 'distinct loop' gets stronger rather than weaker.

Screenshot follow-on: the new content provides new hero frames for the store listing that only Vela can show: a season map ('Chapter 3 of 7 · The Hard Day'), a chapter with a proof woven into the text and highlighted, a future-self letter quoting real dated proofs, and a guided session screen with its soundscape. Make sure screenshot inputs cover verb-shaped and 'I…' desires once the shaper ships.

plan.vision:
Vela 1.1, "Night Atlas", turns Vela from a text-only story app into the one manifestation app that visibly remembers what you did. Each dream gets its own night sky, generated on the phone. Each chapter is a narrated scene in a seven-chapter season that runs from a first glimpse to becoming. Each step you take toward the dream becomes a star, and its position, light and sentence come from you. The next chapter is built from that proof, and the proof is highlighted in gold inside the story. The sky also lives outside the app: today's bridge on the Lock Screen, your constellation on the Home Screen, and a reminder at your ritual time that quotes the sentence you wrote. Nothing is ever taken away. Progress never resets, every chapter is kept in a Memory Book, and the full loop stays free with no account and no servers: unlimited listening, the sky, widgets and a private backup. Vela Plus adds room for more than one dream, Deep chapters, original soundscapes and keepsakes.

People will want it because it is the opposite of the category's pattern. Competitors ask a 20-question interrogation, put a weekly paywall in front, and serve interchangeable pastel stories built on stock photos. Vela is beautiful in a way only the user's own data can make it, gives them something real to do today, and shows them, star by star, that they did it. That same distinctiveness is the Guideline 4.3 defence. Every new surface shows the imagine → act → prove → adapt loop, not generic manifestation content.
plan.visual_system:
NIGHT ATLAS: VISUAL SYSTEM v2
The language is celestial navigation and the star atlas. It is built on Vela, the constellation of the Sails, and on the existing sail-and-star app icon. It is not a "galaxy" app. Decoration is limited to engraved chart line-work and the user's own data drawn as stars. That keeps it clear of Stella's pastel look, Soul's glowing figures, and Magnetic's black-and-gold.

1) BACKGROUND
components/sky/SkyBackdrop.tsx is mounted once in app/_layout.tsx behind the Stack and Tabs. Scenes are transparent (Stack contentStyle and Tabs sceneStyle backgroundColor 'transparent'; verify this on day 1 under the native-stack fade). Everything is react-native-svg 15.15.4, which is already installed, so it renders the same on react-native-web.
- L0: a vertical gradient from sky800 #110F2A to sky950 #05040D, plus a horizon RadialGradient covering the bottom 30% at 15–30% alpha. The horizon is tinted by the active dream's focus: Love #3A2147, Abundance #3A2A22, Career #1C2B4A, Health #123A3A, Confidence #2A2160, Peace #1A2E4F. Morning-ritual users get a dawn hint, #F2A27C at 8%.
- L1: a seeded starfield of 140 circles. Radii are 0.6, 1.0 and 1.6; opacities are .35, .6 and .9. It uses mulberry32 (reuse lib/story/rng) seeded from hash(profile.createdAt + name), so every user's sky is unique and stable. It is one memoized Svg.
- L2: chart line-work at 5–7% alpha: 3 declination arcs, 4 meridians and a tick scale on one edge.
- L3: two nebula RadialGradients, violet #A897FF and teal #6FD3C1 at 8–10%, drifting ±16px over 24s.
- Only 10 stars twinkle: an Animated.View opacity loop between 0.35 and 1 over 2.4–5.6s. Scroll parallax runs at 0.15, 0.3 and 0.5 of the scroll offset through a SkyScroll context.
- Variants: calm (default); reveal (line-work at 12%, used for the Weave and Star Birth); reader (nebula off, stars at 50% for legibility); still (all motion frozen, for screenshots).
- Chapter plates are generated per dream and season by the same generator, seeded by intentId + season. Each shows the horizon tint, the focus-area sign, the chapter numeral and that season's proof stars. There are no stock photos and no AI images of people anywhere.

2) COLOUR TOKENS
These replace the colors in constants/theme.ts. bg stays #0B0A18, and the old token names are kept as aliases so untouched screens still compile.
- SKY (60%): sky950 #05040D, sky900 #0B0A18, sky800 #110F2A, sky700 #19163A (card base, used at 72% alpha), sky600 #241F52 (pressed).
- STARLIGHT TEXT (30%), one hue in four tiers: ink100 rgba(246,242,255,1), ink80 .80, ink64 .64, ink48 .48. ink48 is the floor on the sky (about 4.6:1). Cards need ink56 or higher (about 5.7:1). The .38 tier is deleted.
- LOOP GRAMMAR (≤10%), used identically everywhere:
  - GOLD = the future: gold500 #E9B44C is the ONE filled CTA per viewport. gold300 #F5D58E is for numerals, the user's own words and selected borders. goldEngrave rgba(233,180,76,.24) is for hairlines and plate corners. onGold is #1E1503.
  - VIOLET = the bridge: violet400 #A897FF, with violetWash rgba(168,151,255,.10) for bridge cards. The bridge CTA is filled violet with sky950 text, so the loop's action is never a text link.
  - STARLIGHT = proof: did #FFF3D6 (warm), moved #EEF0FF (cool), learned #C9D8FF (pale blue). Kind is shown by tint and by glyph shape, never by gold. starGlow is rgba(255,236,190,.35).
- Lines: hairline rgba(214,206,255,.10), chartLine rgba(214,206,255,.06). Danger #E8938F is used for destructive actions only.
- Rules:
  - Delete the success green and the gold-wash accentSoft fills, which turn brown on indigo.
  - Selected state = sky700 surface + 1.5px gold300 border + gold icon + 18px check badge.
  - Shadows are tinted sky950 at 60%, never grey. The gold glow (r16, .35) belongs to the primary button only.

3) TYPE
- SERIF, the voice of the future: @expo-google-fonts/newsreader@0.4.1 (Newsreader_400Regular, Newsreader_400Regular_Italic).
- SANS, the UI voice: @expo-google-fonts/instrument-sans@0.4.2 (InstrumentSans_400Regular, InstrumentSans_600SemiBold).
- Loading: expo-font@57.0.1 useFonts in the root layout (web and native), with first render gated on load. On iOS the fonts are also embedded through the expo-font config plugin so there is no flash of unstyled text. Web screenshots then match iOS; today web renders Times.
- Scale, following the skill's limit of 4 sizes and 2 weights (400 and 600):
  - Display 32/38, Newsreader 400, tracking -0.3: chapter titles, greetings, ceremonies.
  - Title 22/28, Newsreader 400: screen and card titles.
  - Body 17/26 in Instrument Sans 400 for UI; story reading in Newsreader 400 at 17/28. The reader's S/M/L setting (17/19/21) is an accessibility option, not part of the design scale.
  - Caption 13/18 in Instrument Sans 400. Eyebrows use 600, uppercase, +1.2 tracking.
- The user's own words are Newsreader Italic in gold300 inside curly quotes. Writing inputs use italic placeholders at weight 400, never 600.
- Counts use fontVariant ['tabular-nums']. Verify Instrument Sans has tnum; if not, fall back to Newsreader numerals.
- Georgia and the generic 'serif' fallback are banned. A <T variant='display|title|body|reading|caption|eyebrow'> component is the only way to set text. A CI grep fails any fontSize or hex literal in app/.
- Store captions only: Newsreader SemiBold 600, used by the compositor and never shipped in the app.

4) MATERIALS
There are three, and only three.
- (a) OPEN SKY: no container. Used for story text, affirmations and the constellation.
- (b) VELLUM card: sky700 at 72%, 1px hairline, 1px top highlight rgba(255,255,255,.06), radius 20, padding 24.
- (c) GILDED PLATE: used only for the hero chapter card, chapter plates and the finale. sky800 → sky700 gradient, a 1px gradient stroke in goldEngrave (bright top-left, fading out), four L-shaped corner ticks in gold300, and an inset mini constellation.

Buttons:
- Primary: gold500 pill, 56pt, 1px inner top highlight rgba(255,255,255,.35), gold glow.
- Bridge: violet400, filled.
- Secondary: 1px gold300 outline.
- Tertiary: ink80 text.

Other:
- Tab bar: sky950 at 92% with a top hairline. No blur, because blur breaks headless capture.
- Inputs: on focus, a gold300 1.5px border and soft glow. outlineStyle 'none' on web.
- Spacing follows the 8-point grid (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64). Screen gutter is 24, or 16 below a 380pt width. Tap targets are at least 44pt. Every icon-only control needs an accessibilityLabel.

5) ICONOGRAPHY
- lucide stays only for system chrome (back, close, more, settings), at stroke 1.75.
- Custom SVG set in components/glyphs:
  - VelaMark: the icon's sail and 4-point star as line-art.
  - StarProof: three shapes, one per proof kind.
  - BridgeGlyph: a heading arrow over a horizon line. It replaces the fitness "footprints".
  - ChapterNumeral: Roman numerals.
  - Six original AreaSigns: Love, a binary pair; Abundance, a cluster; Career, an ascending line; Health, a pulse arc; Confidence, a spire; Peace, a gentle arc.
  - Engraved vignettes for empty states: sail, horizon, window, open door.
- Custom tab icons: Today = horizon with star, Arc = open book, Sky = constellation, Rituals = quill.
- The master pattern is the real Vela sail figure. About 8 hand-placed points from γ, δ, κ, λ, μ, φ, ψ Velorum, approximated. Star positions are facts, so they are free to use.

6) MOTION
Reanimated 4.5.1. Under useReducedMotion, everything becomes plain crossfades.
- Durations: tap 120, state change 220, enter 420, reveal 900, ceremony 1800–2600ms.
- Easing: "drift" = Easing.bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1). Press = spring (damping 18, stiffness 160), scale .97. Overshoot is allowed only on Star Birth.
- Story text inks in by sentence: opacity plus a 6px rise, 120ms stagger.
- Line drawing: strokeDashoffset via useAnimatedProps on native, with a segment-opacity fallback on web.
- Haptics (expo-haptics): selection on picks, light on step, soft on chapter reveal, success on proof.
- Still mode (EXPO_PUBLIC_STILL or ?still=1) renders every animation at its end state and uses a fixed clock.

7) SIGNATURE MOMENTS
- FIRST LIGHT: on welcome, the sky fades in and the VelaMark draws itself over 1.6s. Onboarding progress is 6 stars that connect into the sail.
- THE WEAVE: a 2.4s interstitial before every new chapter. The user's words rise, scatter into stars, lines connect, and the chapter numeral resolves. It is honest anticipation, not fake loading, and can be skipped after the first time.
- ENTER: an optional 30s breath ring that expands with the anchor star.
- READING BY STARLIGHT: text sits directly on the sky. While listening, the current sentence is at 100% and the rest at 55%. A horizon progress line runs above the dock. The user's words, and the woven proof tagged "Woven from your proof", glow gold.
- STAR BIRTH: the proof card condenses into a starlight point, arcs over 900ms to its place in the figure, a line draws from the previous star, a success haptic fires, and the caption reads "Proof 4 · charted". A soft original chime plays only if audio is already active.
- NAMED SKY: the 7th proof closes the figure. The user names it (the default comes from the desire, e.g. "The Studio") and it is set into Your Sky.
- LOG SEALED: Today shows a closure plate: date · Chapter III · 1 proof · next ritual 21:00.

8) THEMES (Plus)
Ink (default), Aurora and Dawn. They swap the horizon and nebula tokens only; the gold, violet and starlight grammar never changes.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE SKILL: the skill says to use Skia for custom drawing. Vela uses react-native-svg instead, because every screen must render on react-native-web for preview and capture, and Skia on web needs a multi-MB CanvasKit wasm. expo-blur and the Liquid Glass tabs are skipped for headless-capture fidelity.

STACK AND MODAL ROUTES

CORE LOOP FLOW

plan.content_expansion:
GOAL
Go from about 2.8k words today to about 33k original words in 1.1. All of it is on-device data under 1 MB of text. Every addition hangs off chapter → bridge → proof; the generic affirmation library is deliberately not expanded.

SCHEMA FIRST
A2 commits lib/story/content/types.ts on day 1. Content agents A3 and A4 write only data files that match it. Each file opens with a style header.

1) DESIRE SHAPER (code; A2)
- Detects the shape: noun phrase; 'to'-verb; bare or imperative verb ('Find my soulmate'); 'I am/I have…' clause; 'I want…'.
- Strips want-verbs and deadline tails ('by next summer', 'this year', 'before my wedding').
- Swaps my→your, I am→you are, me→you.
- Uses a table of about 150 verbs with past and gerund forms.
- Exposes three slots:
  - {desire.quote}: the exact words in curly quotes; always safe.
  - {desire.np}: 'finding your soulmate', 'your own design studio'.
  - {desire.done}: 'you found your soulmate', 'you are debt free'.
- The 9 arrival frames that break today (ar-ca3, ar-ca6, ar-co2, ar-co4, ar-co6, ar-pe1, ar-pe2, ar-he2, ar-love6) are rewritten.
- The intake microcopy becomes 'Say it however it comes out.'

2) SEASONS (A3 writes shared + love/abundance/career; A4 writes health/confidence/peace)
Seven stages:
- I The First Glimpse: the first morning inside it.
- II The Night Before: rehearsal.
- III The Hard Day: something goes wrong and you handle it. This is realistic, and different from every competitor.
- IV Someone Notices.
- V The Threshold: the first 60 seconds after the news.
- VI An Ordinary Day: integration.
- VII Becoming.
Each stage has 6 beats.
- Shared beats (opening-morning, opening-evening, sensory, reflection, closing-morning, closing-evening): 7 stages × 6 beats × 5 variants = 210 fragments.
- Focus beats (stage-arrival, stage-living): 7 × 2 × 6 focus areas × 4 = 336 fragments.
- That is about 546 fragments at about 30 words, roughly 16k words.
- Titles: 7 stages × 6 focus × 3 = 126 titles, shown as 'Chapter III · The Hard Day'.
- Standard chapters are 380–460 words (about 2.5–3 minutes at rate 0.88).
- A morning ritual ends with heading into the day carrying the bridge. An evening ritual ends in rest. The se9 'Evening light' fragment is removed from the morning sequence.

3) MOTIF LEXICON (A4)
24 archetypes, matched on the device by keyword:
- own business/studio; bakery/café/food; creative work (art, music, writing a book); promotion/leadership; new job/career change; freelancing/clients; exam/degree
- debt-free; savings/house deposit; home/apartment; relocation/new country/visa; travel
- partner (romance); wedding; family/baby; family repair; friendship/community
- running/race; strength/fitness; healing/recovery; sleep/rest
- public speaking/visibility; confidence at work; calm mind
Each archetype has 6 sensory details, 3 living moments and 2 witness lines: 264 lines, about 4k words. Love content splits into romance, family and friendship by motif, so no partner is assumed unless the motif is romance.

4) PROOF WEAVE LIBRARY (A3)
- 3 kinds × 3 positions (arrival, witness, pre-closing) × 6 variants = 54 lines. Example (did): 'You remember the afternoon you {proof.done} — this morning began there.'
- 12 recall-by-date lines ('Twelve days ago you wrote {proof.quote}.')
- 8 cumulative lines ('Reality has answered you four times now.')
- 6 'not today → learned' lines
- 6 Scenes-caption lines ('On the wall, the picture you pinned — {scene.quote} —')
About 2k words in total. Each proof is woven once (wovenInChapterId); older proofs return only through recall lines.

5) BRIDGE LIBRARY (A4)
- 25 per focus (150 in total). Each is tagged with a tier (2-minute, 15-minute, brave), a stage, and optionally a motif ('Sketch the sign above your studio door').
- 3 reshape alternates per focus.
- 6 learned-retry prompts.
- About 3k words.

6) THE LETTER BACK + CAPSULE (A3)
- 6 focus areas × 2 letter skeletons, each with 3 openings, 7 proof-quote frames per kind and 3 closings. Assembled with the user's dated proofs.
- 12 capsule prompts.
- About 2.5k words. Never 'future self' and never outcome guarantees.

7) DEEP MODE, Plus (A3 and A4 split by focus)
- 7 stages × 6 focus extended scene passages of about 120 words each: about 5k words.
- 6 breath and rehearsal scripts of about 150 words each: about 1k words.

8) NOTIFICATION COPY (A4)
- 6 slots × 20 templates = 120, filled from the user's data. No guilt or loss framing.
- About 1.5k words.

9) YOUR LINES (A4)
- 3 kinds × 6 focus × 6 = 108 identity lines (did + career → 'I am someone who ships before I'm ready').
- About 1k words.

10) RITUAL PROMPTS (A4)
- Script prompts: from 12 to 84 (12 per focus plus 12 arc-linked: 'Write the scene just after this chapter ends').
- Gratitude stems: from 9 to 48.
- 3·6·9: 10 phrase suggestions per focus, generated through the shaper.
- Onboarding: 4 desire suggestion chips per focus.
- About 1.5k words.

WRITING RULES (in every file header; enforced by tests where possible)
- Original prose only. Second person, present tense.
- {name} appears at least once and {feeling} at least once per chapter. The desire appears in two forms.
- 'now' at most once per chapter. No hard-coded weekdays. No 'future self'. No health, medical or money guarantees. No gendered pronouns for other people.
- Sentences of 28 words or fewer, TTS-friendly (no parentheses or abbreviations).
- Inclusive: no assumed body, gender or relationship.

TESTS (A2)
- Golden matrix: 30 realistic desires × every slot frame.
- Regex bans: 'to to', 'into to', '\.\.', '!\.', 'my/I' leaking into the narration.
- A 30-chapter run with no back-to-back paragraph or bridge.
- Word-count and reading-time bounds per length.
- Each proof is woven exactly once.

OWNER GATE
Skim 20 random renders per focus before content freeze (about day 9).

DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED
The 120 generic affirmations are not expanded. No 'hard day' or 'sleep' affirmation packs, no moon or astrology copy, no 369-as-hero content, and no specific-person or ex scripts.

On-device behaviour not yet verified: (1) whether expo-speech keeps playing in the background and on silent after setAudioModeAsync, (2) whether onBoundary events arrive on iOS 26 for sentence highlighting, (3) whether the expo-audio lock-screen metadata API exists in 57.0.3, (4) the AAC loop-point gap. Each has a fallback (foreground narration plus a bed; paragraph-level highlighting; no Now Playing; crossfading two players). These are the week-1 device-test priority.

critique.verdict:
The direction is right, but the release is too big and some of its native assumptions are wrong. The plan's diagnosis holds up against the code. I checked these directly: Today renders only `intents[0]` (`app/(tabs)/index.tsx`); the contexts read a stale snapshot (`contexts/StoryContext.tsx`); `futureMemory.dateKey` uses UTC; the evidence screen has the `points.length + 1` bug (`app/evidence/[intentId].tsx:126`); the '1 moments' bug is at index.tsx:129; there are 10 `Alert.alert` calls, 0 `accessibilityLabel`s and 15 distinct font sizes; `reshapeAction` is never called and `mood` is never read; and `bun test` passes 67 tests. Night Atlas, proof highlighted in gold inside the next chapter, and the sky as the record of proof is the correct, 4.3-safe way to elevate Vela.

The plan then tries to ship all of the following in about 3.5 weeks: 13 features, about 33k words of agent-written prose, a new widget extension, background audio, a live data migration, and a full 4-tab rework. Every on-device check is squeezed into the owner's last 5 days.

Several native claims are contradicted by the installed or published package source:
- **Lock-screen controls:** expo-audio 57.0.3 needs `interruptionMode` 'doNotMix' for them; the plan uses 'duckOthers'.
- **Microphone string:** the expo-audio config plugin adds a generic microphone permission text by default.
- **Premium voices:** expo-speech reports them as 'Default', so "prefer Enhanced" skips the best voices.
- **Book of Proof on web:** expo-print on web ignores the HTML and just calls `window.print()`.
- **Background narration:** a JS-timer sentence queue is likely to stall when the phone locks.

The migration also takes each user's stage from a chapter counter that the refresh-icon bug inflated. Adding 'journal' pushes the keywords over Apple's 100-character limit.

Recommendation: ship 1.1 as the trust pass, the visual system, the content engine, the living constellation on Today, the upgraded reader, the new onboarding, the Memory Book, forgiving progress with personal reminders, and the new listing. Run widgets as a parallel 1.1.1 track whose signing spike starts on day 1. Move soundscape breadth, Deep chapters, the Letter Back and capsule, the Book of Proof, themes and the pannable Sky tab to 1.2.

The biggest thing missing for "people want it" is not visual. The signature payoff (your real action woven into the story) only appears after a user leaves, acts and comes back. It should land in session 1, and in App Review's first minute.

gaps.issue: The migration takes each user's stage from the inflated v1 chapter counter. The plan maps existing users to 'stage min(chapter, 7)' and the 'current story to chapter N'. But in v1, `regenerate()` (`C:\Users\Gain John\Downloads\solve_problem\vela\contexts\StoryContext.tsx`) raises `intent.chapter` every time the reader's refresh icon is tapped (`app/story/[id].tsx` `again()`), with no proof. Each tap also adds a new 'open' action without closing the previous one.
gaps.why_it_matters: A v1 user who rerolled 8 times with 1 proof would land at stage VII and the finale holding a one-star figure. Named Sky and the Letter Back assume 7 proofs. Orphaned open actions would show in the Memory Book as a stack of unfinished bridges. This is the one data path where a bug destroys the proof the app is built on.
gaps.fix: Set stage = min(completedProofs + 1, 7) and keep the displayed chapter number separate. Keep only the newest non-completed action per intent as the live bridge, and mark older open ones as lapsed (hidden). Add a reroll-heavy v1 fixture and a fixture with several open actions to the release-blocking migrate tests.

gaps.issue: The audio-session settings contradict each other. In expo-audio 57.0.3 (`build/AudioModule.types.d.ts` line 167), lock-screen controls (`setActiveForLockScreen`) require interruptionMode 'doNotMix'. The plan sets 'duckOthers' and also promises lock-screen Now Playing (soundscapes feature and screenshot frame 6).
gaps.why_it_matters: As specified, either Now Playing silently fails or the mode change is discovered during device QA in the final week.
gaps.fix: Choose 'doNotMix' while a chapter session plays; it is a focused listen, so pausing podcasts is acceptable. That enables lock-screen controls. Alternatively keep 'duckOthers' and drop Now Playing from the scope and the screenshots. Record the decision in a tested `lib/audio/session.ts`.

gaps.issue: Background narration is likely to stall. expo-speech already queues utterances natively (`node_modules/expo-speech/ios/SpeechModule.swift` calls `synthesizer.speak(utterance)`; the JS docs say speak() 'adds an utterance to queue'), but it has no pre/post-utterance delay option. The plan's 350ms paragraph pauses and its JS-driven per-sentence queue therefore depend on timers that may not fire once the screen locks and no bed is playing.
gaps.why_it_matters: Narration could stop after one sentence when the phone is locked. Also, declaring UIBackgroundModes 'audio' when a reviewer cannot hear persistent audio is a known Guideline 2.5.4 rejection. The plan treats background audio as fine 'because real audio plays', but that is only true when a soundscape bed is on.
gaps.fix: Queue the whole chapter as per-sentence utterances in one go, with no JS timers between them. Drive highlighting from each utterance's onStart and onDone, which removes the dependence on onBoundary/iOS 26. Let punctuation provide the pauses. Test locked-screen and silent-switch playback in a TestFlight build within the first 3 days. If it fails, remove UIBackgroundModes instead of shipping it unused. Add 'Tap Listen, then lock the phone' to the review notes.

gaps.issue: The expo-audio config plugin injects a generic microphone permission. `expo-audio@57.0.3 plugin/build/withAudio.js` defaults to NSMicrophoneUsageDescription 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your microphone', recordAudioAndroid=true and enableBackgroundPlayback=true. The plan lists 'expo-audio' as a plugin with no options.
gaps.why_it_matters: Vela would ship a vague microphone permission text it never uses. It also undercuts the privacy story, and background mode gets enabled by default whether or not it was verified.
gaps.fix: Configure the plugin explicitly (microphonePermission, recordAudioAndroid: false, and enableBackgroundPlayback tied to the result of the audio spike). Unzip the release-candidate IPA and check the built Info.plist in CI.

gaps.issue: Premium voices are invisible. expo-speech maps only `.enhanced` to 'Enhanced' (`SpeechModule.swift`, getVoices), so iOS Premium voices, the best ones, come back as 'Default'. The plan's 'prefers Enhanced English voices' and frame 6's 'Enhanced · Ava' are built on that field.
gaps.why_it_matters: The voice is the biggest gap in perceived quality against server-TTS competitors, and the picker would steer users away from the voices that sound best.
gaps.fix: Rank voices by identifier substring (premium > enhanced > compact) and show each voice's real name. Make the 'download a better voice' hint plain text instructions (Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content > Voices). Never use an App-Prefs: URL, which is private API and a 2.5.1 rejection risk.

gaps.issue: One global SkyBackdrop behind transparent native-stack screens is unproven, and it breaks for modals. The root Stack in `app/_layout.tsx` uses animation 'fade'. With transparent screens, a crossfade shows both screens' text overlapping. iOS modal and pageSheet presentations (the IA's paywall and capsule/seal modals) live in a separate presentation container and will not see a backdrop mounted behind the Stack. The web preview uses a JS stack, so it will not reveal either problem. The single SkyScroll parallax context also jumps when switching tabs.
gaps.why_it_matters: The whole visual system rests on this layer. If it fails on device after Phase 2 screens are built, every screen has to be reworked.
gaps.fix: Make the `<Screen>` primitive own the backdrop from day 1. Default to a per-screen opaque backdrop: a module-level memoized static starfield, with twinkle only while the screen is focused (useIsFocused). Try the global transparent approach only after an on-device check in the first TestFlight build. Drop the scroll parallax.

gaps.issue: Sentence-by-sentence ink-in and in-paragraph effects cannot be built as specified. In React Native, nested `<Text>` spans cannot take transforms or Reanimated entering animations, so 'opacity plus a 6px rise per sentence, 120ms stagger' would force each sentence into its own block Text and break inline text flow. Nested spans also do not report their position, which auto-scrolling to the current sentence needs.
gaps.why_it_matters: The reader is the product's peak screen. Discovering this in Phase 2 forces a redesign under deadline.
gaps.fix: In the T/Reading contract: animate the rise per paragraph; do sentence highlighting and gold user-word spans through nested Text color/opacity state only; auto-scroll by paragraph using onLayout.

gaps.issue: Custom-font weight and italic handling is missing from the type system. With custom font families, fontWeight '600' and fontStyle 'italic' do not select the 600 or Italic files: iOS and Android fall back or synthesize, and web fakes the italic. `theme.ts` `type.display` and `type.title` carry fontWeight '600' and are spread across 15 screens, and the plan keeps old tokens as aliases 'so untouched screens still compile'.
gaps.why_it_matters: Expect wrong weights, fake italics on the user's own words (the gold-italic signature), and differences between web screenshots and iOS. That defeats the stated goal of making web match iOS.
gaps.fix: `<T>` maps each variant to an explicit family (Newsreader_400Regular_Italic, InstrumentSans_600SemiBold) and strips fontWeight and fontStyle. Extend the lint grep to ban fontWeight and fontStyle in app/. Gating render on useFonts is enough; the expo-font plugin embedding is redundant. Also, the 4 TTFs total about 0.4 MB, not 0.9 MB (the 400 files are 68 KB and 116 KB), which I measured from the tarballs.

gaps.issue: Kept chapters will grow into one large AsyncStorage value. `vela.arcs.v2` stores every chapter's full text and highlight spans in one JSON that the persist queue rewrites on every bridge choice, proof, rename and rest.
gaps.why_it_matters: At about 3 KB per chapter, that is roughly 1 MB a year. It would be serialized on the JS thread at the exact moment Star Birth animates, which is jank on low-end iPhones. On web, localStorage is capped at about 5 MB.
gaps.fix: Use an index key plus one immutable key per chapter, and write after the ceremony finishes (InteractionManager). Add a size and perf test to A2's suite.

gaps.issue: Daypart is baked in at weave time. Chapters are woven when the proof is saved, at any hour, and stored. But they are read later ('Save for 21:00'), and the engine picks 'daypart open and close based on ritual time and the current hour'.
gaps.why_it_matters: A morning opening and an 'into the day' closing read in bed at 21:00 breaks the immersion the whole release is selling.
gaps.fix: Store both opening/closing variants and pick one when the chapter is opened, or choose from the ritual setting only. Exclude daypart from the persisted text.

gaps.issue: The chapter-length numbers do not add up, and the content quality gate is unrealistic. 546 fragments at about 16k words is about 30 words per fragment. A 6-beat skeleton plus the proof beat, the 'Previously' opener and motif lines comes to about 250–300 words, not 380–460. Deep's 42 passages of about 120 words add roughly 120 words per chapter, not +500, so '6–8 minutes' will not hold. The owner skim (20 renders × 6 focus areas × about 420 words) means reading roughly 50k words.
gaps.why_it_matters: Either chapters ship at about 2 minutes while the listing promises more, or the content agents discover mid-sprint that they need about twice the words. Agent-written prose is also exactly the 'AI slop' that low-star reviews punish Moonly for.
gaps.fix: Fix the target length first and size the pools from it. Replace the skim with this: the owner reads one full season for 2 focus areas (14 chapters). Add an automated style lint for LLM tells (em-dash density, 'not X but Y', stock words such as whisper or tapestry), a read-aloud TTS pass, and the golden matrix.

gaps.issue: Prompts collide at proofs 1 and 2. The plan asks for notification permission after the first Star Birth, shows the AddWidget sheet after the second, shows the soft Plus nudge 'after the 2nd proof', and leaves the review prompt ambiguous. `lib/reviewPrompt.ts` currently fires the rating prompt after the second proof from the evidence screen. Asking for notifications only after a proof also means users who never act are never asked.
gaps.why_it_matters: Three or four asks stacked on the same peak moment turns the Star Birth into a pop-up gauntlet. It also hides reminders from the users who most need them.
gaps.fix: Add `lib/asks.ts`, pure and tested, which allows at most one ask per session in a fixed priority order. Move the notification ask to the moment the user commits a bridge or sets an if-then time ('Remind me at 9am to do this?').

gaps.issue: Deep links and notification taps on cold start are not covered. The plan specifies 'a response listener', which misses the notification tap that launched the app. `RootNavigator` (`app/_layout.tsx`) waits only for UserContext, not story data, so a cold-start `vela://story/<id>` renders 'This story has drifted off.' (`app/story/[id].tsx`) until StoryContext loads. Navigating before the Stack mounts also throws.
gaps.why_it_matters: Notifications and widgets are the plan's retention engine, and they all enter the app through cold-start deep links.
gaps.fix: Use useLastNotificationResponse and route only after every store is ready. Make RootNavigator wait for ArcContext as well. Add cold-start deep-link checks to the simulator harness.

gaps.issue: Personal text on the Lock Screen. The accessoryRectangular widget shows the bridge, and notifications quote the user's proof and desire. Desires can be very private (debt, health, a relationship).
gaps.why_it_matters: Exposing private desires to anyone glancing at a locked phone contradicts the 'Private by design' frame and creates 1-star risk.
gaps.fix: Apply `.privacySensitive()` to desire and proof text in widgets. Add a 'Keep my words off the Lock Screen' setting, on by default for Lock Screen surfaces, which switches to neutral copy.

gaps.issue: The widget build is missing a privacy manifest and a silent-failure guard. The plan's app.json section has no `ios.privacyManifests` entry. Scripture Mate needed UserDefaults reason 1C8F.1 for its App Group, and the extension reading UserDefaults(suiteName:) needs its own PrivacyInfo. The plan also copies Scripture Mate's `requireOptionalNativeModule('ExtensionStorage')` pattern, which, per memory, hid a skipped pod across two shipped releases.
gaps.why_it_matters: Risk of an ITMS-91053 upload rejection, and of widgets shipping with no live data while every test stays green.
gaps.fix: Add both privacy manifests. Add a CI release gate that fails unless the IPA contains 'ExtensionStorage' and the log shows 'Installing ExtensionStorage'. Show widget-write failures in a dev diagnostics screen instead of no-op'ing them.

gaps.issue: The keywords overflow. The current field in `store/localizations/en-US.strings` is 99 characters; adding ',journal' makes it 107, over Apple's 100. `scripts/check_metadata.py` runs in `ios-release.yml`.
gaps.why_it_matters: The release build fails at the metadata step, or the field gets truncated by hand under pressure.
gaps.fix: Drop 'goal' or 'assumption'. Also drop 'manifest' once 'Manifestation' is in the name, since Apple indexes name words.

gaps.issue: Still mode could leak into production. EXPO_PUBLIC_STILL is inlined at build time, and still mode freezes motion and fixes the clock at 21:04.
gaps.why_it_matters: A release built with it set ships wrong greetings, wrong date keys and wrong notification scheduling, and nothing fails visibly.
gaps.fix: Honour still mode only when Platform.OS === 'web' and either __DEV__ or ?still=1. Add a guard in `ios-release.yml` that fails the build if EXPO_PUBLIC_STILL is set. Make `lib/clock.ts` injectable only in tests and on web.

gaps.issue: Accessibility and small screens are under-specified. QA runs only at 430×932. The SkyHero is a fixed 320px, so on an iPhone SE (375×667, still supported at the iOS 16.4 minimum) the loop card's one CTA falls below the fold. There is no Dynamic Type plan. SVG stars are not individually accessible, so 'tap a star' and the pannable sky do not work with VoiceOver. Under Reduce Motion, ambient twinkle, drift and parallax should be off, not crossfaded. The ink48 ≈ 4.6:1 contrast figure is correct only on flat sky900 (I recomputed it); over the horizon tint, nebula and stars it falls below 4.5:1.
gaps.why_it_matters: The skill's 375px baseline and its thumb-zone and contrast rules are broken on exactly the screens being redesigned, and an inaccessible sky is the new core visual.
gaps.fix: Add 375×667 and accessibility-size Dynamic Type captures to the PR gates. Size the hero as a clamp of about 30% of window height, with 200px as the floor. Put invisible Pressables with accessibilityLabels over the stars and offer a list alternative. Measure contrast against the lightest sampled backdrop pixel. Under Reduce Motion, render a static sky.

gaps.issue: What happens when Plus lapses is undefined. The plan promises 'everything you made stays readable if Plus ends', but it does not say what happens to a lapsed user with 3 active dreams: which ones keep weaving, and which feed notifications and widgets. PlusContext re-checks the entitlement on every foreground (`onlyIncludeActiveItemsIOS`), so a lapse will happen silently.
gaps.why_it_matters: Without a rule, the code will either lock dreams, breaking the promise, or leave Plus features free.
gaps.fix: Define the rule. On lapse every dream stays readable, the user picks one active dream, and the others rest until re-subscription. Unit-test it in PlusContext and ArcContext.

gaps.issue: Paywall price math and prominence (Guideline 3.1.2). A hard-coded '$29.99/yr ≈ $2.50/mo' is wrong in non-USD storefronts, and the per-month equivalent must be less prominent than the price actually billed.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is a common paywall rejection, and it would show wrong figures to most non-US users.
gaps.fix: Compute the monthly equivalent from StoreKit's numeric price and currency using Intl. Render it smaller than the billed price, and hide it while prices are null.

gaps.issue: Widget screenshots are not producible as planned. Frame 5 needs the real SwiftUI widgets on the Home Screen and Lock Screen. From Windows-only development that means automating the widget gallery on the macOS runner, and the plan does not include that.
